title.zh: 卷三十四 志第二十四 五行一
title.raw: 卷三十四 志第二十四 五行一 Volume 34 Treatises 28: Five Elements 1

sentences.zh: 萬物盈於天地之間，而其為物最大且多者有五：一曰水，二曰火，三曰木，四曰金，五曰土。

translations.literal: The myriad things fill heaven and earth; among them as things, the greatest and most numerous are five: first called water, second fire, third wood, fourth metal, fifth earth.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad things fill heaven and earth, yet among them the greatest and most abundant substances are five: water, fire, wood, metal, and earth.

sentences.zh: 其用於人也，非此五物不能以為生，而闕其一不可，是以聖王重焉。

translations.literal: In their use for mankind, without these five things one cannot live, and lacking any one of them is impossible; therefore the sage kings valued them.
translations.idiomatic: In their application to human life, none of these five can be dispensed with for sustenance; to lack even one is impossible. Hence sage kings held them in esteem.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂五物者，其見象於天也為五星，分位於地也為五方，行於四時也為五德，稟於人也為五常，播於音律為五聲，發於文章為五色，而總其精氣之用謂之五行。

translations.literal: What are called the five things—in their manifestations in heaven they are the five stars, in their apportionment on earth the five directions, in their movement through the four seasons the five virtues, in what people receive the five constants, spread in musical pitch the five tones, expressed in literary ornament the five colors, and gathering their essence and vital force, their use is called the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: These five substances appear in heaven as the five stars, on earth as the five directions, through the four seasons as the five virtues, in human beings as the five constants, in music as the five tones, in literary ornament as the five colors; taken together, the operation of their essential qi is called the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 自三代之後，數術之士興，而為災異之學者務極其說，至舉天地萬物動植，無大小，皆推其類而附之於五物，曰五行之屬。

translations.literal: From after the Three Dynasties, masters of numerology arose, and those who studied calamities and anomalies strove to carry their doctrines to the limit, until they took all things in heaven and earth, animate and inanimate, great and small, and by pushing their kinds attached them to the five things, calling them attributes of the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties, numerologists flourished, and scholars of calamities and portents pushed their theories to extremes, until every creature and plant in heaven and earth, great or small, was classified and assigned to one of the five substances as an attribute of the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 以謂人稟五行之全氣以生，故於物為最靈。

translations.literal: It was held that mankind receives the complete qi of the Five Elements to be born, and therefore among things is most spiritually perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: They held that human beings are born receiving the full qi of the Five Elements and are therefore the most spiritually perceptive of all creatures.

sentences.zh: 其餘動植之類，各得其氣之偏者，其發為英華美實、氣臭滋味、羽毛鱗介、文采剛柔，亦皆得其一氣之盛。

translations.literal: The remaining kinds of animate and inanimate things, each receiving the partial qi, in their manifestations as splendid flowers and fine fruit, odors and flavors, feathers, scales, and shells, literary ornament and hardness or softness—all likewise obtain the fullness of one qi.
translations.idiomatic: Other animate and inanimate kinds each receive a partial allotment of qi; whether in splendid blossoms and fine fruit, scent and flavor, feathers, scales, and shells, or ornament and hardness or softness, each manifests the dominance of a single element.

sentences.zh: 至其為變怪非常，失其本性，則推以事類吉凶影響，其說尤為委曲繁密。

translations.literal: When they became strange transformations beyond the norm and lost their native character, they were pushed by categories of affairs into auspicious or inauspicious omens and influences; these doctrines were especially tortuous and dense.
translations.idiomatic: When things became uncanny anomalies that lost their natural character, scholars deduced categories of events for good or ill omens and influences—a doctrine especially convoluted and elaborate.

sentences.zh: 蓋王者之有天下也，順天地以治人，而取材於萬物以足用。

translations.literal: Generally, when a king possesses the realm, he follows heaven and earth to govern mankind and takes materials from the myriad things to supply needs.
translations.idiomatic: When a king holds the realm, he governs mankind in accord with heaven and earth and draws on the myriad things of creation to meet every need.

sentences.zh: 若政得其道，而取不過度，則天地順成，萬物茂盛，而民以安樂，謂之至治。

translations.literal: If government obtains the Way and taking does not exceed measure, then heaven and earth complete in harmony, the myriad things flourish, and the people are secure and joyful—this is called supreme governance.
translations.idiomatic: If government follows the Way and extraction does not exceed proper bounds, heaven and earth complete their cycles harmoniously, the myriad things flourish, and the people live in security and joy—this is called perfect order.

sentences.zh: 若政失其道，用物傷夭，民被其害而愁苦，則天地之氣沴，三光錯行，陰陽寒暑失節，以為水旱、蝗螟、風雹、雷火、山崩、水溢、泉竭、雪霜不時、雨非其物，或發為氛霧、虹蜺、光怪之類，此天地災異之大者，皆生於亂政。

translations.literal: If government loses the Way, uses things and injures what is young, and the people suffer harm and sorrow, then the qi of heaven and earth is defiled, the three luminaries go astray, yin and yang and cold and heat lose their seasons, producing flood and drought, locusts and caterpillars, wind and hail, thunder and fire, mountains collapsing, waters overflowing, springs drying up, snow and frost out of season, rain not of its proper kind, or issuing as miasmic fog, rainbows, and strange lights—these great calamities and anomalies of heaven and earth all arise from disorderly government.
translations.idiomatic: If government strays from the Way, exploits resources and harms the young, and the people suffer harm and grief, the qi of heaven and earth turns defiled; the sun, moon, and stars go astray; yin and yang and the seasons of cold and heat fall out of step. There come floods and droughts, locusts and caterpillars, wind and hail, thunder and fire, collapsing mountains, overflowing waters, dried-up springs, untimely snow and frost, rain of the wrong substance, or miasmic fog, rainbows, and uncanny lights. These great calamities and portents of heaven and earth all spring from misrule.

sentences.zh: 而考其所發，驗以人事，往往近其所失，而以類至。

translations.literal: Yet in examining what they issued and testing them against human affairs, they often approached what had been lost and arrived by category.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when one examines how such events arise and tests them against human affairs, they often correspond closely to recent failures and arrive by kindred category.

sentences.zh: 然時有推之不能合者，豈非天地之大，固有不可知者邪？

translations.literal: Yet at times there were those that could not be made to fit when pushed—is this not because heaven and earth are vast and inherently have what cannot be known?
translations.idiomatic: Yet at times deductions fail to match—is this not because heaven and earth are so vast that some things must remain unknowable?

sentences.zh: 若其諸物種類，不可勝數，下至細微家人里巷之占，有考於人事而合者，有漠然而無所應者，皆不足道。

translations.literal: As for the kinds of all things, they cannot be numbered; down to the minute divinations of households and lanes—some when tested against human affairs fit, some indifferently have no correspondence—all are not worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: As for the countless kinds of things, down to the petty divinations of households and lanes—some, when checked against human affairs, fit; others correspond to nothing at all. All such cases are not worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「迅雷風烈必變。

translations.literal: A saying runs: "When thunder is sudden and the wind fierce, change is sure to come.
translations.idiomatic: A saying runs: "When thunder is sudden and the wind fierce, change is sure to come.

sentences.zh: 」蓋君子之畏天也，見物有反常而為變者，失其本性，則思其有以致而為之戒懼，雖微不敢忽而已。

translations.literal: " Generally, in the noble man's reverence for heaven, when he sees things that are contrary to the norm and become transformations, losing their native character, he reflects on what may have caused it and takes warning and fear; even what is slight he does not dare neglect.
translations.idiomatic: " The noble man reveres heaven: when he sees things turn abnormal and lose their natural character, he reflects on what may have caused it and takes warning; even the slightest sign he does not dare ignore.

sentences.zh: 至為災異之學者不然，莫不指事以為應。

translations.literal: But those who study calamities and anomalies are not so; none fail to point to affairs as correspondences.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of calamities and portents are not so: they invariably point to specific events as correspondences.

sentences.zh: 及其難合，則旁引曲取而遷就其說。

translations.literal: When they are hard to fit, then by side references and tortuous selection they shift to accommodate their doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: When a case is hard to fit, they draw in side references and tortuous analogies to bend their doctrine to it.

sentences.zh: 蓋自漢儒董仲舒、劉向與其子歆之徒，皆以春秋、洪範為學，而失聖人之本意。

translations.literal: Generally, from the Han scholars Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, and his son Xin and their kind—all took the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Great Plan as their learning, yet lost the sage's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han scholars Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, his son Liu Xin, and their followers—all who took the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Great Plan as their learning—the sage's original intent was lost.

sentences.zh: 至其不通也，父子之言自相戾，可勝歎哉！

translations.literal: As for their lack of coherence, father and son's words contradict each other—how much is there to sigh over!
translations.idiomatic: Their incoherence runs so deep that father and son contradict each other—a cause for endless sighing!

sentences.zh: 昔者箕子為周武王陳禹所有洪範之書，條其事為九類，別其說為九章，謂之「九疇」。

translations.literal: Formerly Jizi presented to King Wu of Zhou the book of the Great Plan that Yu possessed, arranging its matters into nine categories and distinguishing its doctrines into nine chapters, calling them the "Nine Categories."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Jizi presented to King Wu of Zhou the Great Plan that Yu had possessed, arranging its subjects into nine categories and its doctrines into nine chapters, called the "Nine Categories."

sentences.zh: 考其說初不相附屬，而向為五行傳，乃取其五事、皇極、庶證附於五行。

translations.literal: Examining its doctrines, they were at first not mutually subordinate; yet Liu Xiang, in his Commentary on the Five Elements, then took the five affairs, the supreme norm, and the various proofs and attached them to the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, its doctrines were originally not subordinate to one another; yet in his Commentary on the Five Elements, Liu Xiang took the five affairs, the supreme norm, and the various proofs and attached them all to the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 以為八事皆屬五行歟，則至於八政、五紀、三德、稽疑、福、極之類，又不能附。

translations.literal: If one holds that the eight affairs all belong to the Five Elements, then as for the eight policies, five chronologies, three virtues, examination of doubts, blessings, and the norm and the like, they again cannot be attached.
translations.idiomatic: If one claims that all eight affairs belong to the Five Elements, then the eight policies, five chronologies, three virtues, examination of doubts, blessings, and the norm cannot be attached either.

sentences.zh: 至俾洪範之書失其倫理，有以見所謂旁引曲取而遷就其說也。

translations.literal: This went so far as to make the book of the Great Plan lose its order and principle—thereby showing what is called drawing in side references and tortuous selection to shift and accommodate one's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: This made the Great Plan lose its proper order and principle—a clear instance of drawing in side references and tortuous analogies to bend one's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 然自漢以來，未有非之者。

translations.literal: Yet from Han onward, there has been none who rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Han dynasty onward, no one has rejected this approach.

sentences.zh: 又其祥眚禍痾之說，自其數術之學，故略存之，庶幾深識博聞之士有以考而擇焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, the doctrines of auspicious signs, calamities, misfortune, and pestilence derive from their numerological learning; therefore they are briefly preserved, in hope that scholars of deep insight and broad learning may have material by which to examine and choose.
translations.idiomatic: As for doctrines of auspicious signs, calamities, misfortune, and pestilence, they derive from numerological learning and are therefore preserved in brief, so that scholars of deep insight and broad learning may examine them and judge for themselves.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂災者，被於物而可知者也，水旱、螟蝗之類是已。

translations.literal: What are called calamities afflict things and can be known—floods, droughts, locusts, and the like are such.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities are afflictions that strike visible things and can be known—floods, droughts, locusts, and the like.

sentences.zh: 異者，不可知其所以然者也，日食、星孛、五石、六鷁之類是已。

translations.literal: Anomalies are what cannot be known as to why they are so—eclipses of the sun, comets, five stones, six geese, and the like are such.
translations.idiomatic: Anomalies are events whose causes cannot be known—solar eclipses, comets, showers of five stones, flocks of six geese, and the like.

sentences.zh: 孔子於春秋，記災異而不著其事應，蓋慎之也。

translations.literal: Confucius in the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded calamities and anomalies but did not set forth their corresponding affairs—this was caution.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius in the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded calamities and portents but did not spell out their corresponding events—out of caution.

sentences.zh: 以謂天道遠，非諄諄以諭人，而君子見其變，則知天之所以譴告，恐懼脩省而已。

translations.literal: It was held that the Way of Heaven is distant and is not to instruct people with repeated admonition; when the noble man sees its transformations, he knows heaven's purpose in reprimand and admonition, and is only to fear, cultivate, and examine himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven is remote; it does not instruct people with repeated admonitions. When the noble man sees its transformations, he knows that heaven is reprimanding and warning him, and he need only fear, cultivate virtue, and examine himself.

sentences.zh: 若推其事應，則有合有不合，有同有不同。

translations.literal: If one pushes their corresponding affairs, there are those that fit and those that do not, those that are the same and those that differ.
translations.idiomatic: If one deduces corresponding events, some fit and some do not; some match and some differ.

sentences.zh: 至於不合不同，則將使君子怠焉，以為偶然而不懼。

translations.literal: As for those that do not fit or differ, they would make the noble man slack, taking them as chance and not fearing.
translations.idiomatic: When correspondences fail or differ, the noble man may grow slack, treating them as mere chance and ceasing to fear.

sentences.zh: 此其深意也。

translations.literal: This is its deep meaning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the deeper meaning.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖人慎而不言如此，而後世猶為曲說以妄意天，此其不可以傳也。

translations.literal: Generally, the sage was cautious and did not speak thus, yet later ages still made tortuous doctrines to presume upon heaven at will—this is what cannot be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The sage was cautious and did not speak in this way, yet later ages still devised tortuous doctrines to presume upon heaven's will at random—what cannot be handed down.

sentences.zh: 故考次武德以來，略依洪範五行傳，著其災異，而削其事應云。

translations.literal: Therefore, arranging chronologically from Wude onward, following in brief the Commentary on the Five Elements of the Great Plan, the calamities and anomalies are set forth, while their corresponding affairs are cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, events from the Wude era onward are arranged chronologically; following in brief the Commentary on the Five Elements of the Great Plan, calamities and portents are recorded while their supposed corresponding affairs are omitted.

sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「田獵不宿，飲食不享，出入不節，奪民農時，及有姦謀，則木不曲直。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Five Elements says: "If field hunting is not lodged overnight, food and drink are not offered, going out and coming in are without measure, the people's farming seasons are seized, and there are treacherous plots, then wood does not bend straight.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Five Elements says: "When hunting in the fields is not properly lodged, food and drink are not offered in sacrifice, comings and goings lack restraint, the people's farming seasons are seized, and treacherous plots arise, then wood does not bend straight.

sentences.zh: 」謂生不暢茂，多折槁，及為變怪而失其性也。

translations.literal: " This means growth is not flourishing and lush, much is broken and withered, and there are strange transformations that lose their native character.
translations.idiomatic: " This means that growth fails to flourish, much breaks and withers, and things turn into strange anomalies that lose their natural character.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅。

translations.literal: It also says: "When appearance is not respectful, this is called lack of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When appearance is not respectful, this is called lack of reverence.

sentences.zh: 厥咎狂，厥罰常雨，厥極凶。

translations.literal: Its fault is madness, its punishment constant rain, its extreme misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Its fault is madness, its punishment constant rain, its extreme misfortune.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之痾，時則有青眚青祥、鼠妖，惟金沴木。

translations.literal: At times there are clothing omens, at times turtle portents, at times chicken calamities, at times pestilence of the lower body growing on the upper, at times green calamities and green auspices and rat omens—only metal defiles wood.
translations.idiomatic: At times there are omens in clothing, turtle portents, chicken calamities, pestilence in which the lower body grows upon the upper, green calamities and green auspices, and rat omens—only when metal defiles wood.

sentences.zh: 木不曲直。

translations.literal: Wood does not bend straight.
translations.idiomatic: Wood Does Not Bend Straight

sentences.zh: 武德四年，亳州老子祠枯樹復生枝葉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, at the Laozi temple in Bozhou a withered tree again produced branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude (621), at the temple of Laozi in Bozhou a withered tree put forth branches and leaves again.

sentences.zh: 老子，唐祖也。

translations.literal: Laozi is the ancestor of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi was the ancestral sage of Tang.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「枯木復生，權臣執政。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When withered wood revives, a powerful minister holds government.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When withered wood revives, a powerful minister holds the government.

sentences.zh: 」眭孟以為有受命者。

translations.literal: " Sui Meng took it that there was one who had received the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " Sui Meng took this to mean that someone had received the Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，順天門樓東柱已傾毀而自起。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, the eastern pillar of the Shuntian Gate tower, already toppled and destroyed, raised itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year (626), the eastern pillar of the Shuntian Gate tower, though already toppled and ruined, raised itself upright.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「木仆而自起，國之災。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When wood falls prostrate yet raises itself, it is the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When timber falls prostrate yet raises itself, it is a calamity for the state.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年十一月甲申，陰霧凝凍封樹木，數日不解。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day jiashen, of the second year of Yonghui, yin fog congealed into frost and sealed the trees; for several days it did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the eleventh month of the second year of Yonghui (651), yin mists froze and encased the trees; for several days the ice did not melt.

sentences.zh: 劉向以為木少陽，貴臣象。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that wood is lesser yang and is the image of honored ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang held that wood is lesser yang and symbolizes honored ministers.

sentences.zh: 此人將有害，則陰氣脅木先寒，故得雨而冰也。

translations.literal: When such a person is about to do harm, then yin qi presses upon wood and it grows cold first; therefore it receives rain and turns to ice.
translations.idiomatic: When such a person is about to do harm, yin qi presses upon wood and chills it first; hence rain falls and turns to ice upon the trees.

sentences.zh: 亦謂之樹介，介，兵象也。

translations.literal: It is also called tree armor; armor is the image of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: This is also called "tree armor"; armor is the image of weapons.

sentences.zh: 顯慶四年八月，有毛桃樹生李。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Xianqing, a fuzzy peach tree bore plums.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Xianqing (659), a fuzzy peach tree bore plums.

sentences.zh: 李，國姓也。

translations.literal: Li is the surname of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Li was the imperial surname.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「木生異實，國主殃。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When wood bears strange fruit, the ruler of the state suffers misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When wood bears strange fruit, the ruler of the state suffers misfortune.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年十二月癸酉，氛霧終日不解。

translations.literal: On day guiyou of the twelfth month of the first year of Linde, miasmic fog lasted the whole day without clearing.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the twelfth month of the first year of Linde (664), miasmic fog lasted all day without clearing.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day, rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年十一月乙未，昏霧四塞，連夜不解。

translations.literal: On day yiwei of the eleventh month of the third year of Yifeng, dusk fog blocked on all four sides and through the night did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the eleventh month of the third year of Yifeng (678), dusk fog closed in on all sides and did not lift through the night.

sentences.zh: 丙申，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年三月，雨桂子于台州，旬餘乃止。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Chuigong, osmanthus seeds rained on Taizhou; after more than ten days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year of Chuigong (688), osmanthus seeds rained on Taizhou; after more than ten days it ceased.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天雨草木，人多死。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When heaven rains plants, many people die.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When heaven rains plants, many people die.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年十月，萬象神宮側檉杉皆變為柏。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Changshou, beside the Wanxiang Divine Palace all tamarisk and cedar changed into cypress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Changshou (693), beside the Wanxiang Divine Palace all tamarisk and cedar trees turned into cypress.

sentences.zh: 柏貫四時，不改柯易葉，有士君子之操；

translations.literal: Cypress runs through the four seasons, not changing branch or exchanging leaf, having the conduct of the scholar-gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Cypress endures through all four seasons without changing branch or leaf, embodying the conduct of the scholar-gentleman;

sentences.zh: 檉杉柔脆，小人性也。

translations.literal: Tamarisk and cedar are soft and brittle—the nature of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Tamarisk and cedar are soft and brittle—the nature of petty men.

sentences.zh: 象小人居君子之位。

translations.literal: It symbolizes petty men occupying the position of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: It symbolized petty men occupying the positions of gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 延載元年十月癸酉，白霧，木冰。

translations.literal: On day guiyou of the tenth month of the first year of Yanzai, white fog; trees had ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the tenth month of the first year of Yanzai (694), white fog appeared and trees were encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年三月庚申，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On day gengshen of the third month of the fourth year of Jinglong, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the third month of the fourth year of Jinglong (710), rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，高祖故第有柿樹，自天授中枯死，至是復生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, at the former residence of the High Ancestor there was a persimmon tree that had withered and died from the Tianshou era onward; at this time it revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun (711), at the High Ancestor's former residence a persimmon tree that had withered during the Tianshou era (690–692) came back to life.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年六月，蓬州枯楊生李枝，有實，與顯慶中毛桃生李同。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, in Pengzhou a withered poplar produced plum branches with fruit—the same as the fuzzy peach bearing plums in the Xianqing era.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan (733), in Pengzhou a withered poplar put forth plum branches bearing fruit—the same omen as the fuzzy peach that bore plums in the Xianqing era.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，亳州老子祠枯樹復榮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, at the Laozi temple in Bozhou a withered tree flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (741), at the temple of Laozi in Bozhou a withered tree flourished again.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月己巳，寒甚，雨木冰，數日不解。

translations.literal: That year, on day jisi of the eleventh month, the cold was severe; rain froze on the trees, and for several days it did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the jisi day of the eleventh month, the cold was severe; rain froze on the trees, and the ice did not melt for several days.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年三月庚子，夜霜，木有冰。

translations.literal: On day gengzi of the third month of the first year of Yongtai, frost at night; trees had ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the third month of the first year of Yongtai (765), night frost appeared and trees were encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年十一月，紛霧如雪，草木冰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Dali, swirling fog was like snow; grass and trees had ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Dali (767), swirling fog fell like snow and grass and trees were encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 九年，晉州神山縣慶唐觀枯檜復生。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at the Qingtang Abbey in Shenshan County, Jinzhou, a withered cypress revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (774), at the Qingtang Abbey in Shenshan County, Jinzhou, a withered cypress came back to life.

sentences.zh: 興元元年春，亳州真源縣有李樹，植已十四年，其長尺有八寸，至是枝忽上聳，高六尺，周迴如蓋九尺餘。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xingyuan, in Zhenyuan County, Bozhou, there was a plum tree planted already fourteen years; its height was one foot and eight inches; at this time its branches suddenly shot upward, six feet high, circling round like a canopy of more than nine feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Xingyuan (784), in Zhenyuan County, Bozhou, a plum tree planted fourteen years earlier, only a foot and eight inches tall, suddenly sent its branches shooting upward six feet high, spreading in a canopy more than nine feet across.

sentences.zh: 李，國姓也。

translations.literal: Li is the surname of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Li was the imperial surname.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「木生枝聳，國有寇盜。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When wood produces branches that shoot up, the state has bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When wood puts forth branches that shoot upward, the state will suffer raids and banditry.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，中書省枯柳復榮。

translations.literal: " That year, at the Secretariat a withered willow flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: " That year, at the Secretariat a withered willow flourished again.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年十二月，雨木冰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhenyuan, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhenyuan (785), rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，雨木于陳留，十里許，大如指，長寸餘，中空，所下者立如植。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, wood rained on Chenliu for about ten li; large as a finger, more than an inch long, hollow within; what fell stood upright as if planted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year (788), wood rained on Chenliu for about ten li; pieces the size of a finger, a little over an inch long and hollow within, stood upright where they fell as if planted.

sentences.zh: 木生于下，而自上隕者，上下易位之象；

translations.literal: Wood grows from below, yet falls from above—an image of high and low exchanging places;
translations.idiomatic: Wood grows from below yet falls from above—an image of high and low exchanging places;

sentences.zh: 碎而中空者，小人象；

translations.literal: broken and hollow within is the image of petty men;
translations.idiomatic: broken and hollow within symbolizes petty men;

sentences.zh: 如植者，自立之象。

translations.literal: standing as if planted is the image of self-establishment.
translations.idiomatic: standing upright as if planted symbolizes self-establishment.

sentences.zh: 二十年冬，雨木冰。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twentieth year, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twentieth year (804), rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年九月己酉，大雨，樹無風而摧者十五六。

translations.literal: On day jiyou of the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, great rain; trees without wind were broken, fifteen or sixteen of them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (820), in a great downpour fifteen or sixteen trees broke though there was no wind.

sentences.zh: 近木自拔也。

translations.literal: This approximates trees uprooting themselves.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates trees uprooting themselves.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「木自拔，國將亂。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When wood uproots itself, the state is about to fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When wood uproots itself, the state is about to fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年十一月丁丑，雨木冰；

translations.literal: On day dingchou of the eleventh month of the third year of Changqing, rain froze on the trees;
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the eleventh month of the third year of Changqing (823), rain froze on the trees;

sentences.zh: 成都栗樹結實，食之如李。

translations.literal: In Chengdu a chestnut tree bore fruit; eaten, it was like plums.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengdu a chestnut tree bore fruit that tasted like plums when eaten.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年十一月丙申，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On day bingshen of the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli (825), rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，成都李樹生木瓜，空中不實。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, in Chengdu a plum tree bore papaya, hollow within and without fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dahe (829), in Chengdu a plum tree bore papaya that were hollow and without seed.

sentences.zh: 七年十二月丙戌，夜霧，木冰。

translations.literal: On day bingxu of the twelfth month of the seventh year, night fog; trees had ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day of the twelfth month of the seventh year (833), night fog appeared and trees were encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 開成四年九月辛丑，雨雪，木冰。

translations.literal: On day xinchou of the ninth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng, rain and snow; trees had ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the ninth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng (839), rain and snow fell and trees were encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 十月己巳，亦如之。

translations.literal: On day jisi of the tenth month, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the tenth month, the same occurred.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年十二月丁丑，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On day dingchou of the twelfth month of the first year of Huichang, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the twelfth month of the first year of Huichang (841), rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 四年正月己酉，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On day jiyou of the first month of the fourth year, rain froze on the trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the first month of the fourth year (844), rain froze on the trees.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，亦如之。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, the same occurred.

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年四月，成都李實變為木瓜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong, in Chengdu plum fruit changed into papaya.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong (873), in Chengdu plum fruit turned into papaya.

sentences.zh: 時人以為：李，國姓也；

translations.literal: People of the time took it that Li is the surname of the state;
translations.idiomatic: People of the time interpreted this: Li was the imperial surname;

sentences.zh: 變者，國奪於人之象。

translations.literal: change is the image of the state being seized by others.
translations.idiomatic: and change was the image of the state being wrested from its rulers.

sentences.zh: 廣明二年春，眉州有檀樹已枯倒，一夕復生。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Guangming, in Meizhou there was a sandalwood tree already withered and fallen; in one night it revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Guangming (880), in Meizhou a sandalwood tree that had withered and fallen revived overnight.

sentences.zh: 常雨。

translations.literal: Constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Constant Rain

sentences.zh: 武德六年秋，關中久雨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Wude, in Guanzhong there was prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year of Wude (623), Guanzhong suffered prolonged rain.

sentences.zh: 少陽曰暘，少陰曰雨，陽德衰則陰氣勝，故常雨。

translations.literal: Lesser yang is called drought; lesser yin is called rain. When yang virtue declines, yin qi prevails; hence constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser yang is drought; lesser yin is rain. When yang virtue declines, yin qi prevails—hence constant rain.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年春，霖雨。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year of Zhenguan (641), soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年八月，京城大雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the capital had great rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Yonghui (655), the capital was deluged.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年八月，霖雨，更九旬乃止。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xianqing, soaking rain; after ninety days more it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Xianqing (656), soaking rain fell and did not cease for another ninety days.

sentences.zh: 開元二年五月壬子，久雨，禜京城門。

translations.literal: On day renzi of the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyuan, prolonged rain; exorcistic rites were performed at the capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyuan (714), prolonged rain fell and exorcistic rites were performed at the capital gates.

sentences.zh: 十六年九月，關中久雨，害稼。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixteenth year, in Guanzhong prolonged rain harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixteenth year (728), prolonged rain in Guanzhong damaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載秋，大雨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Tianbao, great rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of Tianbao (746), great rain fell.

sentences.zh: 十二載八月，久雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year (753), prolonged rain fell.

sentences.zh: 十三載秋，大霖雨，害稼，六旬不止。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, great soaking rain harmed the crops; for sixty days it did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirteenth year (754), great soaking rain damaged the crops and did not cease for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 九月，閉坊市北門，蓋井，禁婦人入街市，祭玄冥太社，禜明德門，壞京城垣屋殆盡，人亦乏食。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the north gates of wards and markets were closed, wells were covered, women were forbidden to enter streets and markets, sacrifices were offered to the Dark Sovereign and the Grand Altar of Soil, exorcistic rites at the Mingde Gate; the capital's walls and houses were nearly all destroyed, and people also lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the north gates of wards and markets were closed, wells covered, and women forbidden from the streets; sacrifices were offered to the Dark Sovereign and the Grand Altar of Soil, and exorcistic rites performed at the Mingde Gate. The capital's walls and houses were nearly all ruined, and the people went hungry.

sentences.zh: 至德二載三月癸亥，大雨，至甲戌乃止。

translations.literal: On day guihai of the third month of the second year of Zhide, great rain; on day jiaxu it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the third month of the second year of Zhide (757), great rain fell and did not cease until the jiaxu day.

sentences.zh: 上元元年四月，雨，訖閏月乃止。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shangyuan, rain; it did not stop until the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Shangyuan (760), rain fell and did not cease until the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，霖雨連月，渠竇生魚。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year, soaking rain for consecutive months; ditches and drains bred fish.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year (761), soaking rain lasted for months on end, and fish appeared in ditches and drains.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年九月丙午，大雨，至于丙寅。

translations.literal: On day bingwu of the ninth month of the first year of Yongtai, great rain; it lasted until day bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the ninth month of the first year of Yongtai (765), great rain fell and continued until the bingyin day.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年四月，雨，至于九月，閉坊市北門，置土臺，臺上置壇，立黃幡以祈晴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Dali, rain; it lasted until the ninth month. The north gates of wards and markets were closed; earthen platforms were set up, altars placed upon them, and yellow banners raised to pray for clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month of the fourth year of Dali (769), rain fell until the ninth month. The north gates of wards and markets were closed; earthen platforms were erected with altars on top and yellow banners raised to pray for clear skies.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，連雨，害秋稼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, consecutive rain harmed the autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year (771), consecutive rain damaged the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年正月乙未，大雨雪，至于庚子，平地數尺，雪上黃黑如塵。

translations.literal: On day yiwei of the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, great rain and snow; it lasted until day gengzi. On level ground it was several feet deep; on the snow were yellow-black marks like dust.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan (786), heavy rain and snow fell until the gengzi day, piling several feet deep on level ground, with yellow-black dust-like stains upon the snow.

sentences.zh: 五月乙巳，雨，至于丙申。

translations.literal: On day yisi of the fifth month, rain; it lasted until day bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the fifth month, rain fell and continued until the bingshen day.

sentences.zh: 時大飢，至是麥將登，復大雨霖，眾心恐懼。

translations.literal: At the time there was great famine; when the wheat was about to ripen, again came great soaking rain, and people's hearts were filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a great famine; just as the wheat was about to ripen, soaking rain fell again, and the people were filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 十年春，雨，至閏四月，間止不過一二日。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, rain; it lasted until the intercalary fourth month, with pauses of no more than one or two days.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year (794), rain fell until the intercalary fourth month, with pauses of no more than a day or two.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，大雨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year, great rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eleventh year (795), great rain fell.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月己未，大霖雨。

translations.literal: On day jiwei of the eighth month of the nineteenth year, great soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the eighth month of the nineteenth year (803), great soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 元和四年四月，冊皇太子寧，以雨霑服罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yuanhe, the investiture of the heir apparent Ning was halted because rain soaked the ceremonial garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yuanhe (809), the investiture of the heir apparent Li Ning was halted when rain soaked the ceremonial garments.

sentences.zh: 十月，再擇日冊，又以雨霑服罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, another day was chosen for investiture, and again it was halted because rain soaked the garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, another date was chosen for the investiture, and again rain soaked the garments and the ceremony was called off.

sentences.zh: 近常雨也。

translations.literal: This approximates constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates constant rain.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，霖雨害稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year, soaking rain harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year (811), soaking rain damaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月，連雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year, consecutive rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twelfth year (817), consecutive rain fell.

sentences.zh: 八月壬申，雨，至于九月戊子。

translations.literal: On day renshen of the eighth month, rain; it lasted until day wuzi of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the eighth month, rain fell and continued until the wuzi day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月癸未，大雨。

translations.literal: On day guiwei of the second month of the fifteenth year, great rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the second month of the fifteenth year (820), great rain fell.

sentences.zh: 八月，久雨，閉坊市北門。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, prolonged rain; the north gates of wards and markets were closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, prolonged rain fell and the north gates of wards and markets were closed.

sentences.zh: 宋、滄、景等州大雨，自六月癸酉至于丁亥，廬舍漂沒殆盡。

translations.literal: In Song, Cang, Jing, and other prefectures great rain; from day guiyou of the sixth month until day dinghai, lodges and houses were nearly all washed away.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Cang, Jing, and other prefectures were deluged; from the guiyou day of the sixth month to the dinghai day, lodges and houses were nearly all swept away.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年六月，雨，至于八月。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Baoli, rain; it lasted until the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth month of the first year of Baoli (825), rain fell until the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 大和四年夏，鄆、曹、濮等州雨，壞城郭廬舍殆盡。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Dahe, in Yun, Cao, Pu, and other prefectures rain destroyed city walls and lodges nearly completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year of Dahe (830), Yun, Cao, Pu, and other prefectures were flooded, and city walls and lodges were nearly all destroyed.

sentences.zh: 五年正月庚子朔，京城陰雪，彌旬。

translations.literal: On the gengzi new moon of the first month of the fifth year, in the capital gloomy snow lasted more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi new moon of the first month of the fifth year (831), gloomy snow blanketed the capital for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 開成五年七月，霖雨，葬文宗，龍輴陷不能進。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Kaicheng, soaking rain; at the burial of Emperor Wenzong the dragon hearse sank and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Kaicheng (840), soaking rain fell; at Emperor Wenzong's burial the dragon hearse sank in the mud and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 大中十年四月，雨，至于九月。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Dazhong, rain; it lasted until the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month of the tenth year of Dazhong (856), rain fell until the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 咸通九年六月，久雨，禜明德門。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Xiantong, prolonged rain; exorcistic rites at the Mingde Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Xiantong (868), prolonged rain fell and exorcistic rites were performed at the Mingde Gate.

sentences.zh: 乾符五年秋，大霖雨，汾、澮及河溢流害稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Qianfu, great soaking rain; the Fen, Huai, and Yellow rivers overflowed and harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of Qianfu (878), great soaking rain fell; the Fen, Huai, and Yellow rivers overflowed and damaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年秋八月，大霖雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the autumn of the first year of Guangming, great soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the autumn of the first year of Guangming (880), great soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 天復元年八月，久雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianfu, prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianfu (901), prolonged rain fell.

sentences.zh: 服妖。

translations.literal: Clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: Clothing Omens

sentences.zh: 唐初，宮人乘馬者，依周舊儀，著羃䍦，全身障蔽，永徽後，乃用帷帽，施裙及頸，頗為淺露，至神龍末，羃䍦始絕，皆婦人預事之象。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, palace women who rode horses, following the old Zhou ritual, wore veiled hats that screened the whole body. After Yonghui they used curtained hats with skirts reaching the neck, which were rather shallowly revealing. By the end of the Shenlong era veiled hats ceased entirely—all images of women presuming over affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang, palace women who rode horses wore veiled hats per the old Zhou ritual, screening the entire body. After the Yonghui era they used curtained hats with skirts to the neck, rather more revealing. By the end of the Shenlong era veiled hats disappeared entirely—all omens of women intruding into public affairs.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫无忌以烏羊毛為渾脫氈帽，人多效之，謂之「趙公渾脫」。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji made a felt hat of black sheep's wool called "Huntuo"; many imitated it, calling it "Duke Zhao's Huntuo."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji made a felt hat of black sheep's wool called a "huntuo"; many imitated it, calling it "Duke Zhao's Huntuo."

sentences.zh: 近服妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗內宴，太平公主紫衫、玉帶、皂羅折上巾，具紛礪七事，歌舞于帝前。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong once held an inner banquet; Princess Taiping wore a purple robe, jade belt, and black gauze folded-up turban, equipped with the seven items of military harness, and sang and danced before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once held a palace banquet at which Princess Taiping appeared in a purple robe, jade belt, and black gauze military turban, fully equipped with the seven items of military harness, and sang and danced before the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝與武后笑曰：「女子不可為武官，何為此裝束？

translations.literal: The emperor and Empress Wu laughed and said: "A woman cannot be a military officer—why this attire?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Empress Wu laughed and said, "A woman cannot serve as a military officer—why this attire?

sentences.zh: 」近服妖也。

translations.literal: " This approximates clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: " This approximates clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 武后時，嬖臣張易之為母臧作七寶帳，有魚龍鸞鳳之形，仍為象牀、犀簟。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, the favorite Zhang Yizhi made for his mother Zang a canopy of the seven treasures with forms of fish, dragons, phoenixes, and luan birds, and also an ivory bed and rhinoceros mat.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign, the favorite Zhang Yizhi made his mother Zang a canopy of the seven treasures adorned with dragons, fish, phoenixes, and luan birds, along with an ivory bed and rhinoceros mat.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主使尚方合百鳥毛織二裙，正視為一色，傍視為一色，日中為一色，影中為一色，而百鳥之狀皆見，以其一獻韋后。

translations.literal: Princess Anle had the Palace Workshops combine the feathers of a hundred birds to weave two skirts—viewed straight on one color, viewed sideways another, in sunlight one color, in shadow another—yet the forms of all hundred birds were visible; she presented one to Empress Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle had the Palace Workshops weave two skirts from the feathers of a hundred birds—one hue viewed head-on, another from the side, another in sunlight, another in shadow—yet every bird's form was visible; she presented one to Empress Wei.

sentences.zh: 公主又以百獸毛為韀面，韋后則集鳥毛為之，皆具其鳥獸狀，工費巨萬。

translations.literal: The princess also made facing-cloths of the fur of a hundred beasts; Empress Wei gathered bird feathers for hers—all showing the forms of birds and beasts, at a cost of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The princess also made facing-cloths from the fur of a hundred beasts; Empress Wei used gathered bird feathers—each displaying the forms of birds and beasts, at a cost of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 公主初出降，益州獻單絲碧羅籠裙，縷金為花鳥，細如絲髮，大如黍米，眼鼻觜甲皆備，瞭視者方見之。

translations.literal: When the princess first went out to marry, Yizhou presented a cage-skirt of single-thread blue gauze with gold filigree as flowers and birds, fine as silk hair and large as millet grains, eyes, nose, beak, and claws all complete—only one who looked closely could see them.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess first married, Yizhou presented a cage-skirt of single-thread blue gauze with gold filigree flowers and birds, fine as silk thread and no larger than millet grains, with eyes, nose, beak, and claws all complete—visible only to one who looked closely.

sentences.zh: 皆服妖也。

translations.literal: All are clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: All were clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 自作毛裙，貴臣富家多效之，江、嶺奇禽異獸毛羽採之殆盡。

translations.literal: She herself made fur skirts; honored ministers and wealthy families widely imitated her, and the feathers and fur of rare birds and beasts of the Yangzi and Ling ranges were nearly all collected.
translations.idiomatic: She herself made fur skirts; honored ministers and wealthy families widely imitated her, until the feathers and fur of rare birds and beasts of the Yangzi and Ling ranges were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 韋后妹嘗為豹頭枕以辟邪，白澤枕以辟魅，伏熊枕以宜男，亦服妖也。

translations.literal: Empress Wei's younger sister once made a leopard-head pillow to ward off evil, a white-unicorn pillow to ward off demons, and a crouching-bear pillow to bring sons—also clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei's younger sister once made a leopard-head pillow to ward off evil, a white-unicorn pillow to ward off demons, and a crouching-bear pillow to bring sons—all clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年十一月，郊祀，韋后為亞獻，以婦人為齋娘，以祭祀之服執事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Jinglong, at the suburban sacrifice Empress Wei was secondary offerer; women served as fast maidens and performed the rites in sacrificial garb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Jinglong (709), at the suburban sacrifice Empress Wei served as secondary offerer; women served as fast maidens and performed the rites in sacrificial garb.

sentences.zh: 近服妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 中宗賜宰臣宗楚客等巾子樣，其制高而踣，即帝在藩邸時冠也，故時人號「英王踣」。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong bestowed on the chief minister Zong Chuke and others a pattern for caps—high in form and toppling—which was the crown the emperor wore when at his princely residence; hence people of the time called it "Prince Ying's Topple."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong bestowed on Chief Minister Zong Chuke and others a cap pattern—tall and toppling—that the emperor had worn as Prince of Ying; people called it "Prince Ying's Topple."

sentences.zh: 踣，顛仆也。

translations.literal: Topple means to fall prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: "Topple" means to fall prostrate.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年正月，道士尹愔為諫議大夫，衣道士服視事，亦服妖也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, the Daoist Yin Yin became Remonstrance Grand Master and attended to duties in Daoist robes—also a clothing omen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan (737), the Daoist Yin Yin was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master and conducted office in Daoist robes—a clothing omen.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，貴族及士民好為胡服胡帽，婦人則簪步搖釵，衿袖窄小。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, nobles and commoners alike favored Turkic dress and Turkic hats; women pinned swaying-step hairpins, with collars and sleeves narrow and small.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, nobles and commoners alike favored foreign dress and foreign hats; women wore swaying-step hairpins, with narrow collars and sleeves.

sentences.zh: 楊貴妃常以假鬢為首飾，而好服黃裙。

translations.literal: Consort Yang Guifei often used false side-locks as head ornaments and liked to wear yellow skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang Guifei often wore false side-locks as head ornaments and favored yellow skirts.

sentences.zh: 近服妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「義髻拋河裏，黃裙逐水流。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "The righteous topknot cast into the river, the yellow skirt following the water's flow.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time composed a saying: "The righteous topknot cast into the river, the yellow skirt following the water's flow.

sentences.zh: 元和末，婦人為圓鬟椎髻，不設鬢飾，不施朱粉，惟以烏膏注脣，狀似悲啼者。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, women wore round buns and chignon knots, set no side-lock ornaments, applied no rouge or powder, and only blackened the lips with dark paste, looking as if weeping in grief.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era, women wore round buns and chignon knots, forwent side-lock ornaments and rouge, and blackened their lips with dark paste so that they looked as if weeping.

sentences.zh: 圓鬟者，上不自樹也；

translations.literal: Round buns mean the top does not raise itself;
translations.idiomatic: Round buns symbolized that the top does not raise itself;

sentences.zh: 悲啼者，憂恤象也。

translations.literal: weeping in grief is the image of sorrow and care.
translations.idiomatic: weeping in grief symbolized sorrow and distress.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，吳、越間織高頭草履，纖如綾縠，前代所無。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wenzong, between Wu and Yue they wove high-headed straw sandals fine as gauze silk—unheard of in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wenzong's reign, the Wu and Yue regions wove high-headed straw sandals fine as gauze silk—unheard of in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 履，下物也，織草為之，又非正服，而被以文飾，蓋陰斜闒茸泰侈之象。

translations.literal: Sandals are lower things; to weave grass for them, and moreover not proper dress, yet adorn them with ornament—this is roughly the image of yin askew, dissolute excess, and extravagant overreach.
translations.idiomatic: Sandals are humble footwear; to weave grass for them, and moreover not proper dress, yet adorn them with ornament—this symbolized yin askew, dissolute excess, and extravagant overreach.

sentences.zh: 乾符五年，雒陽人為帽，皆冠軍士所冠者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianfu, people of Luoyang made hats all patterned on those worn by Champion soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qianfu (878), the people of Luoyang made hats patterned on those worn by Champion soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又內臣有刻木象頭以裏幞頭，百官效之，工門如市，度木斫之曰：「此斫尚書頭，此斫將軍頭，此斫軍容頭。

translations.literal: Moreover, inner courtiers carved wooden elephant heads to line their futou; the hundred officials imitated them, and craftsmen's gates were like markets. Measuring the wood as they carved, they said: "This one chops a Minister's head, this one a General's head, this one a Army Supervisor's head.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, inner courtiers carved wooden elephant heads to line their official caps; officials imitated them until craftsmen's shops thronged like markets. As they carved, they would say, "This one chops a Minister's head, this one a General's head, this one an Army Supervisor's head.

sentences.zh: 」近服妖也。

translations.literal: " This approximates clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: " This approximates clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 僖宗時，內人束髮極急，及在成都，蜀婦人效之，時謂為「囚髻」。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xizong, inner palace women bound their hair extremely tight; when at Chengdu, Shu women imitated them, and people called it the "prisoner's bun."
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xizong's reign, palace women bound their hair extremely tight; when the court reached Chengdu, Shu women imitated them, and people called it the "prisoner's bun."

sentences.zh: 唐末，京都婦人梳髮以兩鬢抱面，狀如椎髻，時謂之「拋家髻」。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, capital women combed their hair with both side-locks embracing the face, shaped like chignon knots; people called it the "abandoning-home bun."
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tang, capital women combed their hair with both side-locks framing the face in chignon shape; people called it the "abandoning-home bun."

sentences.zh: 又世俗尚以琉璃為釵釧。

translations.literal: Moreover, the common world favored using glass for hairpins and bracelets.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the common people favored glass hairpins and bracelets.

sentences.zh: 近服妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates clothing omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates clothing omens.

sentences.zh: 拋家、流離，皆播遷之兆云。

translations.literal: "Abandoning home" and "wandering in exile" are both omens of being driven from one's place, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: "Abandoning home" and "wandering in exile" were both omens of displacement, it was said.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，十六宅諸王以華侈相尚，巾幘各自為制度，都人傚之，則曰：「為我作某王頭。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhaozong, the princes of the Sixteen Residences vied in splendor and extravagance, each devising his own style of cap; capital people imitated them and would say: "Make me such-and-such Prince's head.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhaozong's reign, the princes of the Sixteen Residences vied in splendor, each devising his own cap style; capital people imitated them and would say, "Make me Prince So-and-so's head.

sentences.zh: 」識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: " Those with insight took it as inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Those with insight took this as inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 龜孽。

translations.literal: Turtle portents.
translations.idiomatic: Turtle Portents

sentences.zh: 大足初，虔州獲龜，六眼，一夕而失。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazu, in Qianzhou a turtle was caught with six eyes; in one night it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazu era (701), in Qianzhou a six-eyed turtle was caught; overnight it vanished.

sentences.zh: 肅宗上元二年，有鼉聚于揚州城門上，節度使鄧景山以問族弟珽，對曰：「鼉，介物，兵象也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan of Emperor Suzong, alligators gathered on the Yangzhou city gate. Military Governor Deng Jingshan asked his clansman younger brother Bing, who replied: "The alligator is a shelled creature—the image of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan (761), alligators gathered on the Yangzhou city gate. Military Governor Deng Jingshan asked his clansman Deng Bing, who replied, "The alligator is a shelled creature—the image of war.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，潤州魚鼈蔽江而下，皆無首。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, in Runzhou fish and turtles covered the river flowing downstream, all without heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan (787), in Runzhou fish and turtles covered the river flowing downstream, all headless.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，魏博管內有蟲，狀如龜，其鳴晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, within the Weibo circuit there was an insect shaped like a turtle; its cry day and night did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dahe (829), within the Weibo circuit an insect shaped like a turtle cried day and night without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 近龜孽也。

translations.literal: This approximates turtle portents.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates turtle portents.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權在蔡州，州中地忽裂，有石出，高五六尺，廣袤丈餘，正如大龜。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan was at Caizhou, the ground in the prefecture suddenly split and a stone emerged, five or six feet high and more than a zhang in breadth and length, just like a great turtle.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan held Caizhou, the ground suddenly split and a stone emerged five or six feet high and more than a zhang across, shaped exactly like a great turtle.

sentences.zh: 雞禍。

translations.literal: Chicken calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken Calamities

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年七月，冀州雌雞化為雄。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Chuigong, in Jizhou a hen changed into a rooster.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Chuigong (687), in Jizhou a hen changed into a rooster.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年正月，明州雌雞化為雄。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yongchang, in Mingzhou a hen changed into a rooster.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yongchang (689), in Mingzhou a hen changed into a rooster.

sentences.zh: 八月，松州雌雞化為雄。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, in Songzhou a hen changed into a rooster.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, in Songzhou a hen changed into a rooster.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年春，滑州匡城縣民家雞有三足。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jinglong, in Kuangcheng County, Huazhou, a commoner's household had a chicken with three feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jinglong (708), in Kuangcheng County, Huazhou, a commoner's chicken had three feet.

sentences.zh: 京房易妖占曰：「君用婦言，則雞生妖。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Book of Changes omen divination says: "When the ruler employs women's counsel, then chickens produce omens.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes omen divination says, "When the ruler heeds women's counsel, chickens produce omens.

sentences.zh: 玄宗好鬬雞，貴臣、外戚皆尚之，貧者或弄木雞，識者以為：雞，酉屬，帝生之歲也；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong loved cockfighting; eminent officials and affinal kin all prized it, and the poor might toy with wooden chickens; the knowing held that the chicken is of the you attribute—the year of the emperor's birth;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was fond of cockfighting; eminent officials and imperial affines all took it up, while the poor might amuse themselves with wooden cocks. The knowing observed that the rooster belongs to the you branch—the year of the emperor's birth;

sentences.zh: 鬬者，兵象。

translations.literal: Fighting is the image of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting is the image of war.

sentences.zh: 近雞禍也。

translations.literal: This approximates chicken calamities.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates chicken calamities.

sentences.zh: 大中八年九月，考城縣民家雄雞化為雌，伏子而雄鳴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dazhong, in a commoner's household in Kaocheng County a rooster changed into a hen, brooded chicks, yet crowed as a male.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dazhong (854), in a commoner's household in Kaocheng County a rooster changed into a hen, brooded chicks, yet crowed as a male.

sentences.zh: 化為雌，王室將卑之象，反雌伏也。

translations.literal: Changing into female is the image of the royal house about to be lowered—reverting to female submission.
translations.idiomatic: Its change into a female signified that the royal house would be lowered—a reversion to female submissiveness.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝時，雌雞化為雄，至元帝而王氏始萌，蓋馴致其禍也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuandi of Han, a hen changed into a rooster; by the time of Emperor Yuandi the Wang clan first sprouted—likely gradually leading to that calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuandi of Han a hen changed into a rooster; by Emperor Yuandi's reign the Wang clan had begun to rise—likely the gradual prelude to their calamity.

sentences.zh: 咸通六年七月，徐州彭城民家雞生角。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Xiantong, in a commoner's household in Pengcheng, Xuzhou, a chicken grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Xiantong (865), in a commoner's household in Pengcheng, Xuzhou, a chicken grew horns.

sentences.zh: 角，兵象，雞，小畜，猶賤類也。

translations.literal: Horns are the image of warfare; the chicken is a small domestic beast—still a base sort.
translations.idiomatic: Horns betoken war; the chicken is but a small domestic beast—a creature of base rank.

sentences.zh: 下體生上之痾。

translations.literal: Pestilence in which the lower body grows upon the upper.
translations.idiomatic: Lower Body Growing on Upper Pestilence

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年七月，宋州襄邑有獵者得雉，五足，三足出背上。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong, in Xiangyi, Songzhou, a hunter obtained a pheasant with five feet—three feet emerging from its back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong (873), in Xiangyi, Songzhou, a hunter took a pheasant with five feet, three of them sprouting from its back.

sentences.zh: 足出于背者，下干上之象；

translations.literal: Feet issuing from the back is the image of the lower violating the upper;
translations.idiomatic: Feet springing from the back signified the lower encroaching upon the upper;

sentences.zh: 五足者，眾也。

translations.literal: Five feet signifies multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Five feet signified multitude.

sentences.zh: 青眚青祥。

translations.literal: Green calamities and green auspices.
translations.idiomatic: Green Calamities and Green Auspices

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年四月，立晉王為太子，有青氣繞東宮殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, when the Prince of Jin was installed as heir apparent, green qi encircled the Eastern Palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan (643), when the Prince of Jin was installed as crown prince, green vapor encircled the Eastern Palace hall.

sentences.zh: 始冊命而有祲，不祥。

translations.literal: At the very investiture there was a baleful sign—inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: At the very moment of investiture a baleful sign appeared—an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 十八年六月壬戌，有青黑氣廣六尺，貫于辰戌，其長亙天。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year, on the day renxu, there was green-black qi six feet wide, piercing through Chen and Xu; its length spanned heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year (644), on the day renxu, a green-black vapor six feet wide pierced the Chen and Xu sectors, its length spanning the sky.

sentences.zh: 大和九年，鄭注篋中藥化為蠅數萬飛去。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe, the medicine in Zheng Zhu's chest transformed into tens of thousands of flies and flew away.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dahe (835), the medicine in Zheng Zhu's casket transformed into tens of thousands of flies and flew away.

sentences.zh: 注始以藥術進，化為蠅者，敗死之象。

translations.literal: Zhu had first advanced through pharmaceutical arts; transformation into flies is the image of defeat and death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu had risen through pharmaceutical arts; its transformation into flies signified defeat and death.

sentences.zh: 近青眚也。

translations.literal: This approximates green calamities.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates green calamities.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年六月，昏，西北有青氣三。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Qianyuan, at dusk, in the northwest there were three green vapors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Qianyuan (760), at dusk three green vapors appeared in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 鼠妖。

translations.literal: Rat omens.
translations.idiomatic: Rat Omens

sentences.zh: 武德元年秋，李密、王世充隔洛水相拒，密營中鼠，一夕渡水盡去。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Wude, Li Mi and Wang Shichong faced each other across the Luo River; in Mi's camp the rats in one night all crossed the water and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Wude (618), Li Mi and Wang Shichong confronted each other across the Luo River; in Mi's camp the rats crossed the river in a single night and all departed.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「鼠無故皆夜去，邑有兵。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When rats without cause all depart at night, the town will have warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When rats without cause all depart at night, the town will face war.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年，建州鼠害稼。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, in Jianzhou rats harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan (639), in Jianzhou rats ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，渝州鼠害稼。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, in Yuzhou rats harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (647), in Yuzhou rats ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，長孫无忌第有大鼠見於庭，月餘出入無常，後忽然死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, at Zhangsun Wuji's residence a great rat appeared in the courtyard; for more than a month it came and went irregularly, then suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing (658), at Zhangsun Wuji's residence a great rat appeared in the courtyard; for more than a month it came and went without pattern, then suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年十一月，洛州猫鼠同處。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Longshuo, in Luozhou cats and rats dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Longshuo (661), in Luozhou cats and rats dwelt together.

sentences.zh: 鼠隱伏象盜竊，猫職捕嚙，而反與鼠同，象司盜者廢職容姦。

translations.literal: The rat's hiding symbolizes thievery; the cat's duty is to catch and bite—yet it instead dwells with rats, the image of those charged with suppressing thieves abandoning their office and tolerating wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: The rat's hiding betokens theft; the cat's office is to catch and bite—yet it dwelt with rats instead, signifying that those charged with suppressing thieves had abandoned their duties and tolerated malfeasance.

sentences.zh: 弘道初，梁州倉有大鼠，長二尺餘，為猫所嚙，數百鼠反嚙猫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongdao, in a Liangzhou granary there was a great rat more than two feet long; a cat bit it, and several hundred rats bit the cat in return.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Hongdao era (683), in a Liangzhou granary there was a great rat over two feet long; a cat bit it, and several hundred rats bit the cat in return.

sentences.zh: 少選，聚萬餘鼠，州遣人捕擊殺之，餘皆去。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter more than ten thousand rats gathered; the prefecture sent men to strike and kill them, and the rest all departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward more than ten thousand rats gathered; the prefecture sent men to strike them down, and the rest dispersed.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，有蛇鼠鬬于右威衞營東街槐樹，蛇為鼠所傷。

translations.literal: During Jingyun, a snake and rats fought in a scholar tree on the east street of the Right Majestic Guard camp; the snake was wounded by the rats.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era (710–712), a snake and rats fought in a locust tree on the east street of the Right Majestic Guard camp, and the snake was wounded by the rats.

sentences.zh: 鬬者，兵象。

translations.literal: Fighting is the image of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting betokens war.

sentences.zh: 景龍元年，基州鼠害稼。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinglong, in Jizhou rats harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinglong (707), in Jizhou rats ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，韶州鼠害稼，千萬為羣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, in Shaozhou rats harmed the crops, numbering tens of millions in swarms.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan (714), in Shaozhou rats ravaged the crops in swarms of tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年十月，魏郡猫鼠同乳。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianbao, in Weijun cats and rats nursed together.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianbao (742), in Weijun cats and rats suckled together.

sentences.zh: 同乳者，甚于同處。

translations.literal: Nursing together surpasses merely dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Nursing together was graver still than merely dwelling together.

sentences.zh: 大曆十三年六月，隴右節度使朱泚於兵家得猫鼠同乳以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Dali, the Longyou Military Governor Zhu Ci obtained cats and rats nursing together from a soldier's household and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Dali (778), the Longyou Military Governor Zhu Ci obtained cats and rats suckling together from a soldier's household and presented them as tribute.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，成都猫鼠相乳。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, in Chengdu cats and rats nursed one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dahe (829), in Chengdu cats and rats suckled one another.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，江西鼠害稼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, in Jiangxi rats harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaicheng (839), in Jiangxi rats ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 咸通十二年正月，汾州孝義縣民家鼠多銜蒿芻巢樹上。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year of Xiantong, in commoners' households in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, many rats carried artemisia and forage to nest in trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year of Xiantong (871), in commoners' households in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, many rats carried artemisia and forage to build nests in trees.

sentences.zh: 鼠穴居，去穴登木，賤人將貴之象。

translations.literal: Rats dwell in burrows; leaving their burrows they ascend trees—the image of base persons about to become honored.
translations.idiomatic: Rats dwell in burrows; leaving their holes to climb trees signified that base persons would rise to honor.

sentences.zh: 乾符三年秋，河東諸州多鼠，穴屋、壞衣，三月止。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Qianfu, in the various prefectures of Hedong there were many rats; they burrowed into houses and ruined clothing—for three months it continued.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year of Qianfu (876), rats swarmed the prefectures of Hedong, burrowing into houses and ruining clothing; the plague lasted three months.

sentences.zh: 鼠，盜也，天戒若曰：「將有盜矣。

translations.literal: The rat is a thief; Heaven's warning seemed to say: "Thieves are about to come.
translations.idiomatic: The rat signifies theft; Heaven's warning seemed to say, "Thieves are coming.

sentences.zh: 乾寧末，陝州有蛇鼠鬬于南門之內，蛇死而鼠亡去。

translations.literal: Late in Qianning, in Shaanzhou a snake and rats fought within the inner south gate; the snake died and the rats vanished and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Qianning era (894–898), in Shaanzhou a snake and rats fought within the inner south gate; the snake died and the rats vanished.

sentences.zh: 金沴木。

translations.literal: Metal defiles wood.
translations.idiomatic: Metal Defiles Wood

sentences.zh: 武德元年八月戊戌，突厥始畢可汗衙帳無故自壞。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu in the eighth month of the first year of Wude, the Turkic Khan Shibi's yurt court compound collapsed without cause.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu in the eighth month of the first year of Wude (618), the yurt court of the Turkic Khan Shibi collapsed without cause.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，金雞竿折。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong assumed the throne, the golden rooster pole snapped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, the golden rooster pole snapped.

sentences.zh: 樹雞竿所以肆赦，始發大號而雞竿折，不祥。

translations.literal: The erected rooster pole is to proclaim amnesty; at the very issuance of the great proclamation the rooster pole snapped—inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The golden rooster pole was erected to proclaim amnesty; as the great proclamation was first issued the pole snapped—an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，有羣狐入御史大夫李承嘉第，其堂無故壞；

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era, a pack of foxes entered the mansion of Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia, and his hall collapsed for no reason;
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era (705–707), a pack of foxes entered the mansion of Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia, and his hall collapsed without cause;

sentences.zh: 又秉筆而管直裂，易之又裂。

translations.literal: Moreover when he took up the brush the tube split straight through, and when replaced it split again.
translations.idiomatic: When he next took up his brush, the pen tube split straight through; a replacement split again.

sentences.zh: 開元五年正月癸卯，太廟四室壞。

translations.literal: In the first month, on the guimao day, of the fifth year of Kaiyuan, four chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year of Kaiyuan (717), on the guimao day, four chambers of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載十二月，哥舒翰帥師守潼關，前軍啟行，牙門旗至坊門，觸落槍刃，眾以為不祥。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, Geshu Han commanded troops defending Tong Pass; when the vanguard set out and the command pennant reached the ward gate, it brushed against a spear blade and fell—the host took it as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao (755), Geshu Han commanded troops at Tong Pass; as the vanguard marched out, the command pennant reached the ward gate, struck a spear blade, and fell—the troops took it as ill omen.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年三月辛酉，中書敕庫壞。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the xinyou day, of the second year of Yongtai, the Secretariat edict archive collapsed.
