translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Yongtai (766), on the xinyou day, the Secretariat edict archive collapsed.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年正月庚戌朔，德宗御含元殿受朝賀，質明，殿階及欄檻三十餘間自壞，衞士死者十餘人。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month, gengxu, of the fourth year of Zhenyuan, Emperor Dezong attended morning congratulations at Hanyuan Hall; at daybreak more than thirty sections of hall steps and balustrades collapsed by themselves, and more than ten guardsmen were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the new year's dawn of the fourth year of Zhenyuan (788), the gengxu day of the first month, Emperor Dezong received court congratulations at Hanyuan Hall; at daybreak more than thirty sections of steps and balustrades collapsed by themselves, killing more than ten guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 含元路寢，大朝會之所御也；

translations.literal: Hanyuan was the approach hall and sleeping palace, where great court assemblies were held;
translations.idiomatic: Hanyuan was the approach hall and sleeping palace, the seat of great court assemblies;

sentences.zh: 正月朔，一歲之元。

translations.literal: The first day of the first month is the origin of the year.
translations.idiomatic: The first day of the first month is the year's beginning.

sentences.zh: 王者之事，天所以儆者重矣。

translations.literal: For a king's affairs, heaven's warning in this was weighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: For the affairs of a sovereign, heaven's admonition in this was weighty indeed.

sentences.zh: 大和九年，鄭注為鳳翔節度使，將之鎮，出開遠門，旗竿折。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe, Zheng Zhu was made military commissioner of Fengxiang; as he was about to depart for his command and went out through Kaiyuan Gate, the flagpole broke.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dahe (835), Zheng Zhu was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang; as he set out for his command and passed through Kaiyuan Gate, the flagpole broke.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，揚州府署門屋自壞，故隋之行臺門也，制度甚宏麗云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, the gate-house of Yangzhou prefectural headquarters collapsed by itself—it had been the Sui dynasty's Branch Secretariat gate, and its design was said to have been very grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangqi (885), the gate-house of the Yangzhou prefectural headquarters collapsed by itself—it had been the Sui Branch Secretariat gate, and its design was said to have been magnificent.

sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「棄法律，逐功臣，殺太子，以妾為妻，則火不炎上。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Five Elements says: "If laws are abandoned, meritorious ministers expelled, the crown prince killed, and a concubine made wife, then fire does not blaze upward.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Five Elements says: "When laws are abandoned, meritorious ministers driven away, the crown prince killed, and a concubine raised to wife, then fire does not blaze upward.

sentences.zh: 」謂火失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: " This means fire lost its nature and became calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " This means that fire lost its nature and turned into calamity.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「上不儉，下不節，盛火數起，燔宮室。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When above is not frugal and below is not restrained, burning fires arise repeatedly and palace chambers are consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When those above are not frugal and those below lack restraint, fierce fires arise repeatedly and palace halls are consumed.

sentences.zh: 」蓋火主禮云。

translations.literal: " For fire governs ritual, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: " For fire governs ritual, it is said.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「視之不明，是謂不哲。

translations.literal: It also says: "When sight is not clear, this is called lacking wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When sight is not clear, this is called lacking wisdom.

sentences.zh: 厥咎舒，厥罰常燠，厥極疾。

translations.literal: Its fault is laxity, its punishment constant heat, its extreme illness.
translations.idiomatic: Its fault is laxity, its punishment constant heat, its extreme illness.

sentences.zh: 時則有草妖，時則有羽蟲之孽，時則有羊禍，時則有目痾，時則有赤眚赤祥，惟水沴火。

translations.literal: At times there are grass omens, at times winged-insect portents, at times sheep calamities, at times eye pestilence, at times red calamities and red auspices—only when water defiles fire.
translations.idiomatic: At times there are grass omens, winged-insect portents, sheep calamities, eye pestilence, and red calamities and red auspices—only when water defiles fire.

sentences.zh: 火不炎上。

translations.literal: Fire does not blaze upward.
translations.idiomatic: Fire Does Not Blaze Upward

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年正月癸巳，武德殿北院火。

translations.literal: In the first month, on the guisi day, of the fourth year of Zhenguan, fire broke out in the northern court of Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Zhenguan (630), on the guisi day, fire broke out in the northern court of Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月壬寅，雲陽石燃，方丈，晝則如灰，夜則有光，投草木則焚，歷年乃止。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the renyin day, of the thirteenth year, stone at Yunyang burned over a square zhang; by day it was like ash, by night it gave light, and when grass or wood were cast upon it they burned; only after years did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year (639), on the renyin day, stone at Yunyang burned over a square zhang; by day it looked like ash, by night it glowed, and whatever grass or wood was thrown upon it caught fire—the burning lasted years.

sentences.zh: 火失其性而沴金也。

translations.literal: Fire had lost its nature and defiled metal.
translations.idiomatic: Fire had lost its nature and was defiling metal.

sentences.zh: 二十三年三月，甲弩庫火。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-third year, the crossbow-armory caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-third year (649), the crossbow-armory caught fire.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年十二月乙巳，尚書司勳庫火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the yisi day, of the fifth year of Yonghui, the Ministry of Personnel merit-records archive caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yonghui (654), on the yisi day, the Ministry of Personnel merit-records archive caught fire.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年九月戊辰，恩州、吉州火，焚倉廩、甲仗、民居二百餘家。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, of the first year of Xianqing, Enzhou and Jizhou suffered fire that burned granaries, armor, and more than two hundred commoners' households.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Xianqing (656), on the wuchen day, Enzhou and Jizhou suffered fire that burned granaries, armor stores, and more than two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十一月己巳，饒州火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the jisi day, Raozhou suffered fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jisi day, Raozhou suffered fire.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年正月丙申夜，明堂火，武太后欲避正殿，徹樂。

translations.literal: On the bingshen night of the first month of the first year of Zhengsheng, the Bright Hall caught fire; Empress Wu wished to avoid the main hall and cancel music.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen night of the first month of the first year of Zhengsheng (695), the Bright Hall caught fire; Empress Wu wished to withdraw from the main hall and suspend music.

sentences.zh: 宰相姚璹以為火因人，非天災也，不宜貶損。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yao Shuan held that the fire was caused by men and was not heaven's calamity, and that one should not demean oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yao Shuan held that the fire was man-made, not a calamity sent by heaven, and that the court should not humble itself.

sentences.zh: 后乃御端門觀酺，引建章故事，復作明堂以厭之。

translations.literal: The empress then attended Duan Gate to watch the feast, citing the Jianzhang precedent, and rebuilt the Bright Hall to overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then attended Duan Gate to watch the feast, citing the Jianzhang precedent, and rebuilt the Bright Hall to overcome the omen.

sentences.zh: 是歲，內庫災，燔二百餘區。

translations.literal: That year the inner treasury suffered disaster, and more than two hundred sections were burned.
translations.idiomatic: That year the inner treasury burned, consuming more than two hundred sections.

sentences.zh: 萬歲登封元年三月壬寅，撫州火。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the renyin day, of the first year of Wansui Dengfeng, Fuzhou suffered fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Wansui Dengfeng (696), on the renyin day, Fuzhou suffered fire.

sentences.zh: 久視元年八月壬子，平州火，燔千餘家。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the renzi day, of the first year of Jiushi, Pingzhou suffered fire that burned more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Jiushi (700), on the renzi day, Pingzhou suffered fire that burned more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年二月，東都凌空觀災。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Jinglong, the Lingkong Abbey of the Eastern Capital suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year of Jinglong (710), the Lingkong Abbey of the Eastern Capital burned.

sentences.zh: 開元五年十一月乙卯，定陵寢殿火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, of the fifth year of Kaiyuan, the sleeping hall of Dingling mausoleum caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Kaiyuan (717), on the yimao day, the sleeping hall of Dingling mausoleum caught fire.

sentences.zh: 是歲，洪州、潭州災，延燒州署，州人見有物赤而暾暾飛來，旋即火發。

translations.literal: That year Hongzhou and Tanzhou suffered disaster; the blaze spread to burn the prefectural offices, and the people of the prefectures saw something red and gleaming fly toward them—fire broke out at once.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hongzhou and Tanzhou burned; the blaze spread to the prefectural offices, and locals saw a red, gleaming object fly in—fire broke out immediately.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月甲戌，興教門樓柱災。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the jiaxu day, of the fifteenth year, the pillar of Xingjiao Gate tower suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year (727), on the jiaxu day, the pillar of Xingjiao Gate tower burned.

sentences.zh: 是年，衡州災，延燒三百餘家，州人見有物大如甕，赤如燭籠，所至火即發。

translations.literal: That year Hengzhou suffered disaster; the blaze spread to burn more than three hundred households, and the people of the prefecture saw a thing as large as a jar, red as a candle shade—wherever it went, fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hengzhou burned; the blaze spread through more than three hundred households, and locals saw an object as large as a jar, red as a lantern shade—wherever it passed, fire erupted.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月丙寅，大雨雪，俄而雷震，左飛龍廏災。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the bingyin day, of the eighteenth year, great rain and snow fell, then thunder sounded, and the Left Flying Dragon Stud suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighteenth year (730), on the bingyin day, heavy rain and snow fell, then thunder pealed, and the Left Flying Dragon Stud burned.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天火燒廏，兵大起。

translations.literal: Omen divination says: "When heaven's fire burns the stud, great armies rise.
translations.idiomatic: Omen divination says: "When heaven's fire burns the stud, great armies rise.

sentences.zh: 」十月乙丑，東都宮佛光寺火。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month, on the yichou day, Foguang Temple of the Eastern Capital palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month, on the yichou day, Foguang Temple of the Eastern Capital palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年六月，東都應天門觀災，延燒左、右延福門，經日不滅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianbao, the Yingtian Gate abbey of the Eastern Capital suffered disaster; the blaze spread to the left and right Yanfu gates and burned for days without going out.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianbao (743), the Yingtian Gate abbey of the Eastern Capital burned; the blaze spread to the left and right Yanfu gates and burned for days.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「君不思道，天火燔其宮室。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, heaven's fire burns his palace chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, heaven's fire consumes his palace halls.

sentences.zh: 」九載三月，華岳廟災，時帝將封西嶽，以廟災乃止。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the ninth year, the Huayue temple suffered disaster; at the time the emperor was about to enfeoff the Western Peak, and because of the temple disaster he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month of the ninth year (750), the Huayue temple burned; the emperor was then preparing to enfeoff the Western Peak and halted the rite because of the temple fire.

sentences.zh: 十載八月丙辰，武庫災，燔兵器四十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the bingchen day, of the tenth year, the Armory suffered disaster and burned more than four hundred thousand weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the tenth year (751), on the bingchen day, the Armory burned, destroying more than four hundred thousand weapons.

sentences.zh: 武庫，甲兵之本也。

translations.literal: The Armory is the root of armor and arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Armory is the foundation of armor and arms.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年十二月己酉，太府左藏庫火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the jiyou day, of the first year of Baoying, the Grand Treasury left storehouse caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoying (762), on the jiyou day, the Grand Treasury left storehouse caught fire.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年十二月辛卯夜，鄂州大風，火發江中，焚舟三千艘，延及岸上民居二千餘家，死者數千人。

translations.literal: On the xinmao night of the twelfth month of the first year of Guangde, Ezhou suffered a great wind; fire arose in the river and burned three thousand boats, spreading to more than two thousand households on shore, and several thousand people died.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao night of the twelfth month of the first year of Guangde (763), Ezhou suffered a great wind; fire broke out on the river and burned three thousand boats, spreading to more than two thousand shore households—several thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 大曆十年二月，莊嚴寺浮圖災。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year of Dali, the pagoda of Zhuangyan Temple suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year of Dali (775), the pagoda of Zhuangyan Temple burned.

sentences.zh: 初有疾風震電，俄而火從浮圖中出。

translations.literal: At first came fierce wind and thunder; then fire issued from within the pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: At first came fierce wind and thunder; then fire burst from within the pagoda.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，江陵度支院火，焚江東租賦百餘萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, the Jiangling revenue commission office caught fire and burned more than a million [units] of Jiangdong land tax and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan (785), the Jiangling revenue commission office caught fire, destroying more than a million in Jiangdong land tax and tribute payments.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，東都尚書省火。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, the Eastern Capital Secretariat caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan (797), the Eastern Capital Secretariat caught fire.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月，家令寺火。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year, the Household Administration Temple caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan (803), the Household Administration Temple caught fire.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，洪州火，燔民舍萬七千家。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, Hongzhou caught fire and burned seventeen thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Yuanhe (807), Hongzhou caught fire, destroying seventeen thousand households.

sentences.zh: 元和七年六月，鎮州甲仗庫災，主吏坐死者百餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Yuanhe, Zhenzhou armor and weapons storehouse suffered disaster; more than a hundred supervising clerks were put to death for responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Yuanhe (812), the Zhenzhou armor and weapons depot burned; more than a hundred officials in charge were executed.

sentences.zh: 八年，江陵大火。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Jiangling suffered a great fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe (813), Jiangling suffered a great fire.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月甲戌，元陵火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the jiaxu day, of the eleventh year, the Yuan imperial tomb caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Yuanhe (816), on the jiaxu day, Emperor Xianzong's Yuan tomb caught fire.

sentences.zh: 李師道起宮室於鄆州，將謀亂，既成而火。

translations.literal: Li Shidao raised palace chambers at Yunzhou, intending to plot rebellion; when they were completed, fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao built palaces at Yunzhou planning rebellion; when the work was finished, they caught fire.

sentences.zh: 大和二年十一月甲辰，禁中昭德寺火，延至宣政東垣及門下省，宮人死者數百人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the jiachen day, of the second year of Dahe, Zhaode Temple within the Forbidden City caught fire, spreading to the east wall of the Xuanzheng Hall and the Secretariat-Chancellery; several hundred palace women died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Dahe (828), on the jiachen day, Zhaode Temple in the palace burned, spreading to the east wall of the Xuanzheng Hall and the Secretariat-Chancellery; several hundred palace attendants died.

sentences.zh: 三年十月癸丑，仗內火。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the guichou day, fire broke out within the arms-guard quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Dahe (829), on the guichou day, fire broke out in the arms-guard quarters.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，陳州、許州火，燒萬餘家。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, Chenzhou and Xuzhou caught fire and burned more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year of Dahe (830), Chenzhou and Xuzhou caught fire, destroying more than ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 十月，浙西火。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhexi caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Zhexi caught fire.

sentences.zh: 十一月，揚州海陵火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yangzhou and Hailing caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yangzhou and Hailing caught fire.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，揚州火。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year, Yangzhou caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year of Dahe (834), Yangzhou caught fire.

sentences.zh: 皆燔民舍千區。

translations.literal: In each case more than a thousand districts of common dwellings were burned.
translations.idiomatic: In each case more than a thousand wards of dwellings were burned.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，飛龍神駒中廏火。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the jisi day, the central stables of the Feilong Divine Colts caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the jisi day, the central stables of the Feilong Divine Colts caught fire.

sentences.zh: 十月，揚州市火，燔民舍數千區。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Yangzhou city caught fire and burned several thousand districts of common dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Yangzhou city caught fire, destroying several thousand wards of dwellings.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禁中昭成寺火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhaocheng Temple within the Forbidden City caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Zhaocheng Temple in the palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 開成二年六月，徐州火，延燒民居三百餘家。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Kaicheng, Xuzhou caught fire and the blaze spread to more than three hundred civilian dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Kaicheng (837), Xuzhou caught fire, spreading to more than three hundred civilian dwellings.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月乙卯，乾陵火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the yimao day, of the fourth year, the Qian imperial tomb caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng (839), on the yimao day, Emperor Gaozong's Qian tomb caught fire.

sentences.zh: 丁丑晦，揚州市火，燔民舍數千家。

translations.literal: On the last day of the dingchou [cycle], Yangzhou city caught fire and burned several thousand districts of common dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the dingchou cycle, Yangzhou city caught fire, destroying several thousand wards of dwellings.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年五月，潞州市火。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Huichang, Luzhou city caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Huichang (841), Luzhou city caught fire.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，西內神龍寺火；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, Shenlong Temple in the western inner palace caught fire;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Huichang (843), Shenlong Temple in the western inner palace caught fire;

sentences.zh: 萬年縣東市火，焚廬舍甚眾。

translations.literal: The east market of Wannian County caught fire and burned very many lodgings and shops.
translations.idiomatic: The east market of Wannian County caught fire, burning a great many shops and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，葬武宗，辛未，靈駕次三原縣，夜大風，行宮幔城火。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, when burying Emperor Wuzong, on the xinwei day the funerary procession halted at Sanyuan County; at night came a great wind, and the traveling palace curtain-walled compound caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Huichang (846), during Emperor Wuzong's burial, on the xinwei day the spirit carriage halted at Sanyuan County; that night a great wind arose and the mourning encampment's curtain walls caught fire.

sentences.zh: 乾符四年十月，東都聖善寺火。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Qianfu, Shengshan Temple of the Eastern Capital caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Qianfu (877), Shengshan Temple of the Eastern Capital caught fire.

sentences.zh: 大順二年六月乙酉，幽州市樓災，延及數百步。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the yiyou day, of the second year of Dashun, a tower in Youzhou city suffered disaster, the blaze spreading for several hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Dashun (891), on the yiyou day, a tower in Youzhou city burned, spreading for several hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 七月癸丑甲夜，汴州相國寺佛閣災。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the first jia night of the guichou day, the Buddha pavilion of Xiangguo Temple in Bianzhou suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on the first jia watch of the guichou night, the Buddha pavilion of Xiangguo Temple in Bianzhou burned.

sentences.zh: 是日暮，微雨震電，或見有赤塊轉門譙藤網中，周而火作。

translations.literal: That day at dusk came slight rain, thunder, and lightning; some saw a red mass revolving in the vine nets of the gate tower, and when it completed its circuit fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: That evening came light rain, thunder, and lightning; some saw a red mass circling in the vine nets of the gate tower, and when it completed its circuit fire broke out.

sentences.zh: 頃之，赤塊北飛，轉佛閣藤網中，亦周而火作。

translations.literal: Shortly, the red mass flew north, revolving in the Buddha pavilion's vine nets; when it completed its circuit fire broke out again.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the red mass flew north, circling in the Buddha pavilion's vine nets; again when it completed its circuit fire broke out.

sentences.zh: 既而大雨暴至，平地水深數尺，火益甚，延及民居，三日不滅。

translations.literal: Then fierce rain suddenly arrived; standing water in the flat ground was several feet deep, yet the fire grew fiercer, spreading to common dwellings, and for three days did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Then a torrential rain burst upon the city; water several feet deep stood in the streets, yet the fire grew fiercer, spreading to civilian dwellings, and burned for three days without going out.

sentences.zh: 常燠。

translations.literal: Constant heat.
translations.idiomatic: Constant Heat

sentences.zh: 天寶元年冬，無冰。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianbao, there was no ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tianbao (742), there was no ice.

sentences.zh: 先儒以為陰失節也。

translations.literal: The early Confucians held that yin had lost its proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Confucians held that yin had lost its proper season.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「知罪不誅，其罰燠，夏則暑殺人，冬則物華實。

translations.literal: It is also said: "When guilt is known yet not punished, the penalty is heat; in summer then scorching heat kills people, and in winter things flower and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said, "When guilt is known yet goes unpunished, the penalty is heat: in summer scorching heat kills people; in winter plants blossom and bear fruit.

sentences.zh: 」蓋當寒反燠，象宜刑而賞之也。

translations.literal: " For when it should be cold yet heat prevails instead, the image is that punishment ought to be applied yet reward is given instead.
translations.idiomatic: " When it should be cold yet heat prevails, the omen signifies that punishment ought to be applied but reward is given instead.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年夏，大燠。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, great heat prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (798), extreme heat prevailed.

sentences.zh: 元和九年六月，大燠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe, great heat prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe (814), extreme heat prevailed.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年冬，少雪，水不冰凍，草木萌荑如正月。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Changqing, snow was scant, water did not freeze, and plants and trees put forth buds as in the first month [of spring].
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Changqing (822), snow was scant, water did not freeze, and plants and trees sprouted buds as in the first month of spring.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年十一月，暖如仲春。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Guangming, it was warm as in mid-spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Guangming (880), the weather was as mild as mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 草妖。

translations.literal: Grass omens.
translations.idiomatic: Grass Omens

sentences.zh: 武德四年，益州獻芝草如人狀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Yizhou presented lingzhi fungus in the shape of a human being.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude (621), Yizhou presented lingzhi fungus shaped like a human figure.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「王德將衰，下人將起，則有木生為人狀。

translations.literal: Omen divination says: "When the king's virtue is about to decline and the lower people are about to rise, then wood grows in human shape.
translations.idiomatic: Omen divination says, "When the king's virtue is about to decline and the lower orders are about to rise, wood grows in human shape.

sentences.zh: 」草，亦木類也。

translations.literal: " Grass also belongs to the wood category.
translations.idiomatic: " Grass, too, belongs to the wood category.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，岐州郿縣民王上賓家，有苦蕒菜高三尺餘，上廣尺餘，厚二分。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong, at the home of Wang Shangbin, a commoner of Mei County in Qizhou, there was a bitter sow-thistle three feet and more in height, a foot and more across at the top, two fen in thickness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong (708), at the home of Wang Shangbin, a commoner of Mei County in Qizhou, a bitter sow-thistle stood more than three feet tall, more than a foot across at the top, and two fen thick.

sentences.zh: 近草妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates grass omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates grass omens.

sentences.zh: 三年，內出蒜條，上重生蒜。

translations.literal: In the third year, garlic shoots brought out from within the palace grew garlic anew atop them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (709), garlic shoots brought from the inner palace grew new garlic atop them.

sentences.zh: 蒜，惡草也；

translations.literal: Garlic is an evil [omen] plant;
translations.idiomatic: Garlic is an inauspicious plant;

sentences.zh: 重生者，其類眾也。

translations.literal: To grow anew signifies its kind will be numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Regrowth signifies that its kind will multiply.

sentences.zh: 四年，京畿藍田山竹實如麥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, in Lantian County of the metropolitan region, bamboo bore fruit like wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jinglong (710), in Lantian County of the capital region, bamboo bore fruit like wheat grains.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大饑。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "Great famine.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，終南山竹有華，實如麥，嶺南亦然，竹並枯死，是歲大饑，民採食之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, bamboo in the Zhongnan Mountains bore flowers, fruit like wheat; the same in Lingnan; the bamboo all withered and died; that year great famine—the people gathered and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan (714), bamboo in the Zhongnan Mountains flowered, fruiting like wheat; the same occurred in Lingnan. The bamboo all withered and died. That year brought great famine, and the people gathered and ate them.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國中竹、柏枯，不出三年有喪。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When bamboo and cypress in the state wither, within three years there is mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When bamboo and cypress in the state wither, mourning comes within three years.

sentences.zh: 」十七年，睦州竹實。

translations.literal: " In the seventeenth year, Muzhou bamboo bore fruit.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan (729), Muzhou bamboo bore fruit.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，臨川郡人李嘉胤屋柱生芝草，狀如天尊像。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Li Jiayin of Linchuan Commandery had spirit fungus grow on his house pillar, shaped like an image of the Heavenly Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign (742–756), Li Jiayin of Linchuan Commandery found spirit fungus growing on a house pillar, shaped like an image of the Heavenly Worthy.

sentences.zh: 上元二年七月甲辰，延英殿御座上生白芝，一莖三花。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the jiachen day, of the second year of Shangyuan, white fungus grew on the imperial throne of Yanying Hall, one stalk with three flowers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Shangyuan (761), on the jiachen day, white fungus grew on the imperial throne of Yanying Hall—one stalk with three flowers.

sentences.zh: 白，喪象也。

translations.literal: White is the image of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: White is the image of mourning.

sentences.zh: 大和九年冬，鄭注之金帶有菌生。

translations.literal: In winter of the ninth year of Dahe, fungus grew on Zheng Zhu's gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year of Dahe (835), fungus grew on Zheng Zhu's gold belt.

sentences.zh: 近草妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates grass omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates grass omens.

sentences.zh: 開成四年六月，襄州山竹有實成米，民採食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng, bamboo in the Xiangzhou mountains bore fruit like rice; the people gathered and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng (839), bamboo in the Xiangzhou mountains bore fruit like rice, and the people gathered and ate them.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年七月，河中解、永樂生草，葉自相樛結，如旌旗之狀，時人以為「旗子草」。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Guangqi, at Jie and Yongle in Hezhong grass grew with leaves knotting themselves like pennants; people of the time called it "Banner Grass."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Guangqi (885), at Jie and Yongle in Hezhong, grass grew with leaves intertwining like pennants; people called it "Banner Grass."

sentences.zh: 一年七月，鳳翔麟游草生如旗狀。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year, at Linyou in Fengxiang grass grew like banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year (886), at Linyou in Fengxiang, grass grew like banners.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其野有兵。

translations.literal: Divination says: "In the countryside there is warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "In the countryside there is warfare.

sentences.zh: 羽蟲之孽。

translations.literal: Calamities among winged creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities Among Winged Creatures

sentences.zh: 武德初，隋將堯君素守蒲州，有鵲巢其砲機。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, the Sui general Yao Junsu held Pu Prefecture; a magpie nested on his cannon mount.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign (618–626), the Sui general Yao Junsu held Pu Prefecture; a magpie nested on his cannon mount.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年春，齊王祐為齊州刺史，好畜鴨，有狸嚙鴨，頭斷者四十餘。

translations.literal: In spring of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Prince You of Qi was governor of Qizhou, fond of raising ducks; a raccoon dog gnawed ducks—more than forty with severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan (643), Prince You of Qi, governor of Qizhou, was fond of raising ducks; a raccoon dog gnawed them, and more than forty were found with severed heads.

sentences.zh: 是歲四月丙戌，立晉王為太子，雌雉集太極殿前，雄雉集東宮顯德殿前。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month, on the bingxu day, the Prince of Jin was established as heir apparent; hen pheasants gathered before Taiji Hall, cock pheasants before Xiande Hall of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the fourth month on the bingxu day, the Prince of Jin was established as heir apparent; hen pheasants gathered before Taiji Hall, and cock pheasants before Xiande Hall of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太極，三朝所會也。

translations.literal: Taiji is where the Three Assemblies meet.
translations.idiomatic: Taiji Hall is where the Three Assemblies meet.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，宋州人蔡道基舍傍有獸高丈餘，頭類羊，一角，鹿形，馬蹄，牛尾，五色，有翅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui, beside the house of Cai Daoji of Song Prefecture was a beast more than a zhang tall, head like a sheep, one horn, deer form, horse hoofs, ox tail, five colors, with wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yonghui (653), beside the house of Cai Daoji of Song Prefecture stood a beast more than ten feet tall, with a sheep-like head, one horn, a deer's body, horse hoofs, an ox tail, five colors, and wings.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「鳥如畜形者，有大兵。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When birds take livestock form, there is great warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When birds take the form of livestock, great armies rise.

sentences.zh: 」五年七月辛巳，萬年宮有小鳥如雀，生子大如鳲鳩。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year, seventh month, on the xinsi day, at Wannian Palace a small bird like a sparrow gave birth to offspring as large as turtledoves.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year of Yonghui (654), in the seventh month on the xinsi day, at Wannian Palace a small bird like a sparrow gave birth to offspring as large as turtledoves.

sentences.zh: 調露元年，鳴鵽羣飛入塞，相繼蔽野，至二年正月，還復北飛，至靈夏北，悉墮地而死，視之皆無首。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiaolu, screaming owls flew in flocks into the frontier, one after another covering the wilderness; by the first month of the second year they flew north again; reaching north of Ling and Xia they all fell dead on the ground—viewed, all were headless.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiaolu (679), screaming owls flew in flocks into the frontier passes, one after another blotting out the wilderness. By the first month of the second year they flew north again; reaching north of Ling and Xia they all fell dead—every one was headless.

sentences.zh: 文明後，天下屢奏雌雉化為雄，或半化者。

translations.literal: After Wenming, throughout the realm reports repeatedly came of hen pheasants turning into cocks, or half-transformed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wenming reign (684), reports repeatedly came from across the realm of hen pheasants turning into cocks, or half-transformed.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年六月辛巳朔，烏集太極殿梁，驅之不去。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month of the fourth year of Jinglong, on xinsi, crows gathered on the beams of Taiji Hall—driven, they would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month of the fourth year of Jinglong (710), on xinsi, crows gathered on the beams of Taiji Hall and would not leave when driven away.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年十一月戊子，雄雉馴飛泰山齋宮內。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, on the wuzi day, a cock pheasant flew tamely within the Mount Tai fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan (725), on the wuzi day, a cock pheasant flew tamely within the Mount Tai fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 封禪，所以告成功，祀事無重於此者，而野鳥馴飛，不忌禁衞，不祥。

translations.literal: Feng and Shan sacrifices are to announce success—no sacrificial affair is weightier than this, yet a wild bird flew tame inside, heedless of the forbidden guard—inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng and Shan rites announce success to heaven; no sacrifice is weightier. Yet a wild bird flew tamely within, heedless of the forbidden guard—an inauspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 二十五年四月，濮州兩烏、兩鵲、兩鸜鵒同巢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year, in Puzhou two crows, two magpies, and two mynahs shared one nest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan (737), in Puzhou two crows, two magpies, and two mynahs shared one nest.

sentences.zh: 隴州鵲哺慈烏。

translations.literal: In Longzhou a magpie nursed filial crows.
translations.idiomatic: In Longzhou a magpie nursed filial crows.

sentences.zh: 二十八年四月庚辰，慈烏巢宣政殿栱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year, on the gengchen day, filial crows nested on the bracket of Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year of Kaiyuan (740), on the gengchen day, filial crows nested on the bracket of Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，又巢宣政殿栱。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day, again nested on the bracket of Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, they nested again on the bracket of Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，葉縣有鵲巢于車轍中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, in Ye County a magpie nested in wheel ruts.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao (754), in Ye County a magpie nested in wheel ruts.

sentences.zh: 不巢木而巢地，失其所也。

translations.literal: Not nesting in trees but on the ground—they had lost their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Not nesting in trees but on the ground—they had lost their proper place.

sentences.zh: 至德二載三月，安祿山將武令珣圍南陽，有鵲巢于城中砲機者三，雛成乃去。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhide, An Lushan's general Wu Lingxun besieged Nanyang; three times a magpie nested on the cannon mounts in the city—when the chicks were grown it left.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Zhide (757), An Lushan's general Wu Lingxun besieged Nanyang; three times a magpie nested on the cannon mounts in the city, and when the chicks were grown it left.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年九月，武功獲大鳥，肉翅狐首，四足有爪，長四尺餘，毛赤如蝙蝠，羣鳥隨而噪之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dali, at Wugong a great bird was caught—flesh wings, fox head, four feet with claws, more than four chi long, fur red like a bat; flocks of birds followed crying at it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dali (773), at Wugong a great bird was caught—flesh wings, a fox head, four clawed feet, more than four feet long, fur red like a bat's; flocks of birds followed, crying at it.

sentences.zh: 近羽蟲孽也。

translations.literal: This approximates winged-creature calamities.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates winged-creature calamities.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，左羽林軍有鸜鵒乳鵲二。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, in the Left Feathered Forest Army a mynah nursed two magpies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Dali (778), in the Left Feathered Forest Army a mynah nursed two magpies.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年三月，中書省梧桐樹有鵲以泥為巢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan, on a parasol tree at the Secretariat a magpie made a nest of mud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan (788), on a parasol tree at the Secretariat a magpie built a nest of mud.

sentences.zh: 鵲巢知歲次，於羽蟲為有知，今以泥露巢，遇風雨壞矣。

translations.literal: Magpies nesting know the year's turn; among winged creatures they are considered intelligent—now using mud for an exposed nest, meeting wind and rain it was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Magpies know the year's turn when they nest; among winged creatures they are counted intelligent. Yet this one built an exposed nest of mud, and wind and rain destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 是歲夏，鄭、汴境內烏皆羣飛，集魏博田緒、淄青李納境內，銜木為城，高二三尺，方十里。

translations.literal: That summer, within the borders of Zheng and Bian all crows flew in flocks, gathering in the territory of Weibo's Tian Xu and Ziqing's Li Na, carrying wood to make walls two or three chi high, ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, crows throughout Zheng and Bian flew in flocks into the territories of Weibo's Tian Xu and Ziqing's Li Na, carrying wood to build walls two or three feet high and ten li square.

sentences.zh: 緒、納惡而焚之，信宿又然，烏口皆流血。

translations.literal: Xu and Na hated it and burned them; after one or two nights they lit again, crows' mouths all bled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Na hated the omen and burned the structures; within a night or two they caught fire again, and the crows' mouths all bled.

sentences.zh: 九年春，許州鵲哺烏雛。

translations.literal: In spring of the ninth year, in Xuzhou a magpie nursed crow chicks.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year of Zhenyuan (793), in Xuzhou a magpie nursed crow chicks.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，有大鳥飛集宮中，食雜骨數日，獲之，不食死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, a great bird flew and gathered in the palace, ate assorted bones for several days; when caught, it would not eat and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan (794), a great bird flew into the palace and ate assorted bones for several days; when caught, it refused food and died.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未晦，水鳥集左藏庫。

translations.literal: On the last day of the sixth month, xinwei, water birds gathered at the Left Vault.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the sixth month, on xinwei, water birds gathered at the Left Vault.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月，懷州𪄢鵊巢內有黃雀往來哺食。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, within a hawk's nest in Huai Prefecture yellow sparrows came and went nursing and feeding.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan (797), within a hawk's nest in Huai Prefecture yellow sparrows came and went, nursing and feeding.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，有異鳥，色青，類鳩、鵲，見於宋州郊外，所止之處，羣鳥翼衞，朝夕嗛稻粱以哺之，睢陽人適野聚觀者旬日。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fourteenth year, a strange bird, green in color, resembling doves and magpies, appeared in the outskirts of Song Prefecture; where it rested, flocks of birds wing-guarded it; morning and evening they carried rice and grain to feed it; people of Suiyang going to the fields gathered to watch for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (798), a strange green bird resembling doves and magpies appeared in the outskirts of Song Prefecture. Wherever it rested, other birds guarded it with outspread wings; morning and evening they brought rice and grain to feed it. For ten days people of Suiyang going to the fields gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 十八年六月，烏集徐州之滕縣，嗛柴為城，中有白烏一，碧烏一。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year, crows gathered at Teng County in Xuzhou, carrying firewood to make walls; among them one white crow, one jade-green crow.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year of Zhenyuan (802), crows gathered at Teng County in Xuzhou, carrying firewood to build walls; among them were one white crow and one jade-green crow.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，常州鸛巢于平地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, in Changzhou storks nested on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe (806), in Changzhou storks nested on level ground.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，羣烏夜集于太行山上。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, flocks of crows gathered at night on the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Yuanhe (809), flocks of crows gathered at night on the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，淄青府署及城中烏、鵲互取其雛，各以哺子，更相搏擊，不能禁。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirteenth year, at the Ziqing circuit headquarters and in the city crows and magpies took each other's chicks, each to nurse its own young, and fought one another in turn; it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe (818), at the Ziqing circuit headquarters and in the city, crows and magpies seized one another's chicks, each nursing them as their own, and fought in turn without cease.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年十一月丙申，羣烏夜鳴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli, on bingshen, flocks of crows cried at night.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli (825), on bingshen, flocks of crows cried at night.

sentences.zh: 開成元年閏五月丙戌，烏集唐安寺，逾月散。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng, on bingxu, crows gathered at Tang'an Temple; after a month they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng (836), on bingxu, crows gathered at Tang'an Temple; after more than a month they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 雀集玄法寺，燕集蕭望之冢。

translations.literal: Sparrows gathered at Xuanfa Temple; swallows gathered at Xiao Wangzhi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Sparrows gathered at Xuanfa Temple; swallows gathered at the tomb of Xiao Wangzhi.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，真興門外鵲巢於古冢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, outside Zhenxing Gate magpies nested in an ancient tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Kaicheng (837), outside Zhenxing Gate magpies nested in an ancient tomb.

sentences.zh: 鵲巢知避歲，而古占又以高下卜水旱，今不巢于木而穴于冢，不祥。

translations.literal: Magpies nesting know to avoid inauspicious years, and ancient divination also uses height to foretell flood and drought; now they do not nest in trees but burrow in tombs—inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Magpies know to nest away from inauspicious years, and ancient divination also reads the height of nests to foretell flood and drought; now they did not nest in trees but burrowed in tombs—an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 秋，突厥鳥自塞北羣飛入塞。

translations.literal: In autumn, birds of the Turks flew in flocks from north of the frontier into the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, birds from the Turks flew in flocks from beyond the frontier passes into the interior.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，有禿鶖羣飛集禁苑。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, bald coots flew in flocks and gathered in the Forbidden Park.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Kaicheng (840), bald coots flew in flocks and gathered in the Forbidden Park.

sentences.zh: 鶖，水鳥也。

translations.literal: The coot is a water bird.
translations.idiomatic: The coot is a water bird.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年，潞州長子有白頸烏與鵲鬬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huichang, in Changzi in Luzhou a white-necked crow fought with magpies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huichang (841), in Changzi in Luzhou a white-necked crow fought with magpies.

sentences.zh: 大中十年三月，舒州吳塘堰有眾禽成巢，闊七尺，高一尺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Dazhong, at Wutang Dam in Shuzhou many birds formed a nest seven chi wide and one chi high.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year of Dazhong (856), at Wutang Dam in Shuzhou many birds formed a communal nest seven chi wide and one chi high.

sentences.zh: 水禽山鳥，無不馴狎。

translations.literal: Water birds and mountain birds—all were tame.
translations.idiomatic: Water birds and mountain birds alike were tame.

sentences.zh: 中有如人面、綠毛、紺爪觜者，其聲曰「甘」，人謂之甘蟲。

translations.literal: Among them was one like a human face, with green feathers and dark blue claws and beak; its cry was "gan"; people called it the gan insect.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was one with a face like a human's, green plumage, and dark blue claws and beak; its cry was "gan," and people called it the Gan creature.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有鳥非常，來宿于邑中，國有兵，人相食。

translations.literal: Divination says: "When an extraordinary bird comes to lodge in a town, the state will have warfare and people will devour one another.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "When an extraordinary bird comes to lodge within a town, the state will see warfare and people will devour one another.

sentences.zh: 咸通七年，涇州靈臺百里戍有雀生燕，至大俱飛去。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiantong, at Baili garrison in Lingtai, Jingzhou, a sparrow gave birth to a swallow; when grown they all flew away.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiantong (866), at Baili garrison in Lingtai, Jingzhou, a sparrow gave birth to a swallow; when grown they all flew away.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「賊臣在國，厥妖燕生雀。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When a treacherous minister is in the state, the portent is a swallow born of a sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When a treacherous minister is in the state, the portent is a swallow born of a sparrow.

sentences.zh: 」雀生燕同說。

translations.literal: " Sparrows giving birth to swallows follows the same doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: " Sparrows giving birth to swallows follows the same doctrine.

sentences.zh: 十一年夏，雉集河內縣署。

translations.literal: In summer of the eleventh year, pheasants gathered at the Henan county magistrate's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eleventh year of Xiantong (870), pheasants gathered at the Henan county magistrate's office.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，吳、越有異鳥極大，四目三足，鳴山林，其聲曰「羅平」。

translations.literal: During Xiantong, in Wu and Yue an extraordinary bird extremely large, with four eyes and three legs, cried in mountain forests; its call was "luoping."
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era, in Wu and Yue an extraordinary bird of enormous size, with four eyes and three legs, cried in the mountain forests; its call was "luoping."

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國有兵，人相食。

translations.literal: Divination says: "The state will have warfare and people will devour one another.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "The state will see warfare and people will devour one another.

sentences.zh: 乾符四年春，廬江縣北鵲巢于地。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year of Qianfu, north of Lujiang county magpies nested on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Qianfu (877), north of Lujiang county magpies nested on the ground.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，鴟、雉集于偃師南樓及縣署。

translations.literal: In summer of the sixth year, owls and pheasants gathered at Yanshi's south tower and at the county magistrate's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year of Qianfu (879), owls and pheasants gathered at the south tower of Yanshi and at the county magistrate's office.

sentences.zh: 劉向說：「野鳥入處，宮室將空。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's explanation says: "When wild birds enter dwellings, palace halls will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained: "When wild birds enter dwellings, palace halls will stand empty.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年春，絳州翼城縣有鵂鶹鳥羣飛集縣署，眾鳥逐而噪之。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Guangming, in Yicheng county, Jiangzhou, owl-falcon birds flew in flocks and gathered at the county office; many birds chased and clamored at them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Guangming (880), in Yicheng county, Jiangzhou, owl-falcon birds flew in flocks and gathered at the county office, and many birds chased and clamored at them.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年、二年，復如之。

translations.literal: In the first and second years of Guangqi, it happened again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first and second years of Guangqi (885–886), the same thing occurred again.

sentences.zh: 鵂鶹，一名訓狐。

translations.literal: The owl-falcon—also called the training fox.
translations.idiomatic: The owl-falcon is also called the instruction fox.

sentences.zh: 中和元年三月，陳留有烏變為鵲。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhonghe, in Chenliu a crow changed into a magpie.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Zhonghe (881), in Chenliu a crow changed into a magpie.

sentences.zh: 二年，有鵲變為烏。

translations.literal: In the second year, a magpie changed into a crow.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe (882), a magpie changed into a crow.

sentences.zh: 古者以烏卜軍之勝負。

translations.literal: In antiquity crows were used to divine victory or defeat in armies.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity crows were used to divine victory or defeat in armies.

sentences.zh: 烏變為鵲，民從賊之象；

translations.literal: A crow changing into a magpie is the image of the people following bandits;
translations.idiomatic: A crow changing into a magpie betokened the people following rebels;

sentences.zh: 鵲復變為烏，賊復為民之象。

translations.literal: A magpie changing back into a crow is the image of bandits returning to be people.
translations.idiomatic: a magpie changing back into a crow betokened rebels returning to be people again.

sentences.zh: 三年，新安縣吏家捕得雉養之，與雞馴，月餘相與鬬死。

translations.literal: In the third year, a clerk's family in Xin'an county caught a pheasant and raised it; it grew tame with chickens, and after more than a month they fought each other to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhonghe (883), a clerk's family in Xin'an county caught a pheasant and raised it; it grew tame with the chickens, and after more than a month they fought each other to death.

sentences.zh: 四年，臨淮漣水民家鷹化為鵝，而弗能游。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at a commoner's home in Lianshui, Linhuai, a hawk transformed into a goose yet could not swim.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhonghe (884), at a commoner's home in Lianshui, Linhuai, a hawk transformed into a goose yet could not swim.

sentences.zh: 鷹以鷙而擊，武臣象也；

translations.literal: The hawk by fierceness strikes—an image of military ministers;
translations.idiomatic: The hawk strikes through fierceness—the image of military ministers;

sentences.zh: 鵝雖毛羽清潔，而飛不能遠，無搏擊之用，充庖廚而已。

translations.literal: Though the goose's feathers are clean, it cannot fly far, has no use for striking, and serves only to fill the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: though the goose's plumage is clean, it cannot fly far and has no power to strike, serving only to fill the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年十二月，陝州平陸集津山有雉二首向背而連頸者，棲集津倉廡後，數月，羣雉數百來鬬殺之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Guangqi, on Jizhou Pinglu Jijin Mountain there was a pheasant with two heads facing back to back with joined necks; it roosted behind the Jijin warehouse, and after several months several hundred pheasants came and fought and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Guangqi (885), on Jijin Mountain in Pinglu, Shanzhou, there was a pheasant with two heads facing back to back on joined necks; it roosted behind the Jijin warehouse sheds, and after several months several hundred pheasants came and fought and killed it.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，閺鄉、湖城野雉及鳶夜鳴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, in Minxiang and Hucheng wild pheasants and kites cried at night.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Guangqi (886), in Minxiang and Hucheng wild pheasants and kites cried at night.

sentences.zh: 七月，中條山鵲焚其巢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on Zhongtiao Mountain magpies burned their nest.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Guangqi (887), on Zhongtiao Mountain magpies burned their nests.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，鵲復焚巢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, magpies again burned their nests.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Guangqi (888), magpies again burned their nests.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「人君暴虐，鳥焚其舍。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When the ruler is cruel and tyrannical, birds burn their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes Commentary says: "When the ruler is cruel and tyrannical, birds burn their dwellings.

sentences.zh: 」三年十月，慈州仵城梟與鴟鬬相殺。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month of the third year, at Wucheng in Cizhou, owls and horned owls fought and killed each other.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month of the third year of Guangqi (888), at Wucheng in Cizhou, owls and horned owls fought and killed each other.

sentences.zh: 光化二年，幽州節度使劉仁恭屠貝州去，夜有鵂鶹鳥十數飛入帳中，逐去復來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guanghua, after Military Commissioner Liu Rengong of Youzhou slaughtered Beizhou and departed, at night more than a dozen owl-falcon birds flew into his tent; driven away, they returned again.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guanghua (899), after Military Commissioner Liu Rengong of Youzhou slaughtered Beizhou and departed, at night more than a dozen owl-falcon birds flew into his tent; driven off, they returned again.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，有禿鶖鳥巢寢殿隅，帝親射殺之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Zhaozong's reign, bald coots nested in the corner of the sleeping hall; the emperor personally shot and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhaozong's reign, bald coots nested in the corner of the sleeping hall; the emperor personally shot and killed them.

sentences.zh: 天復二年，帝在鳳翔，十一月丁巳，日南至，夜驟風，有烏數千，迄明飛噪，數日不止。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, the emperor was at Fengxiang; on dingsi, the winter solstice, at night a sudden gale arose, and several thousand crows from then until dawn flew and clamored, not stopping for several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu (902), the emperor was at Fengxiang; on dingsi, the winter solstice night, a sudden gale arose, and several thousand crows from then until dawn flew and clamored, not stopping for several days.

sentences.zh: 自車駕在岐，常有烏數萬棲殿前諸樹，岐人謂之神鴉。

translations.literal: Since the imperial carriage was at Qi, there were always tens of thousands of crows roosting in the trees before the halls; people of Qi called them divine crows.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial carriage was at Qizhou, tens of thousands of crows always roosted in the trees before the halls; the people of Qi called them divine crows.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣州有鳥如雉而大，尾有火光如散星，集于戟門，明日大火，曹局皆盡，惟兵械存。

translations.literal: In the third year, in Xuanzhou a bird like a pheasant but large, with tail having firelight like scattered stars, gathered at the halberd gate; the next day a great fire, and all the government offices were consumed—only weapons remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu (903), in Xuanzhou a bird like a pheasant but large, its tail bearing firelight like scattered stars, gathered at the halberd gate; the next day a great fire consumed all the government offices—only weapons remained.

sentences.zh: 羊禍。

translations.literal: Sheep calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep Calamities

sentences.zh: 義寧二年三月丙辰，麟游縣有羔生而無尾。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Yining, on bingchen, in Linyou county lambs were born without tails.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Yining (618), on bingchen, in Linyou county lambs were born without tails.

sentences.zh: 是月乙丑，太原獻羖羊，無頭而不死。

translations.literal: In that month on yichou, Taiyuan presented a ram without a head yet not dead.
translations.idiomatic: That same month on yichou, Taiyuan presented a ram without a head that did not die.

sentences.zh: 開元二年正月，原州獻肉角羊。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Kaiyuan, Yuanzhou presented a horned-flesh sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Kaiyuan (714), Yuanzhou presented a sheep with flesh horns.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，富平縣有肉角羊。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Fuping county had a horned-flesh sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Kaiyuan (714), Fuping county had a sheep with flesh horns.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年春，代州崞縣羊生二首連頸，兩尾。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Huichang, in Guo county, Daizhou, a sheep was born with two heads joined at the neck and two tails.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Huichang (842), in Guo county, Daizhou, a sheep was born with two heads joined at the neck and two tails.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「二首，上不一也。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Two heads—the ruler above is not one.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "Two heads—the ruler above is not one.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年夏，平陶民家羊生羔如犢。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Xiantong, at a commoner's home in Pingtao a sheep bore a lamb like a calf.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Xiantong (862), at a commoner's home in Pingtao a sheep bore a lamb like a calf.

sentences.zh: 乾符二年，洛陽建春門外因暴雨，有物墮地如羖羊，不食，頃之入地中，其跡月餘不滅，或以為雨土也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfu, outside Jianchun Gate in Luoyang, because of a violent rainstorm, something fell to the ground like a ram, would not eat, and shortly entered the ground; its tracks for more than a month did not vanish—some thought it was rain-earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianfu (875), outside Jianchun Gate in Luoyang, after a violent rainstorm something fell to earth like a ram, would not eat, and shortly sank into the ground; its tracks remained more than a month without fading—some thought it was rain-earth.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「當旱。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Drought is due.
translations.idiomatic: Divination says: "Drought is due.

sentences.zh: 赤眚赤祥。

translations.literal: Red calamities and red auspices.
translations.idiomatic: Red Calamities and Red Auspices

sentences.zh: 武德七年，河間王孝恭征輔公祏，宴羣帥于舟中，孝恭以金盌酌江水，將飲之，則化為血。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude, Prince Hejian Xiaogong campaigned against Fu Gongyu; feasting the commanders on a boat, Xiaogong with a golden bowl scooped river water, about to drink it, and it turned to blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wude (624), Prince Hejian Xiaogong campaigned against Fu Gongyu; feasting the commanders aboard a boat, Xiaogong scooped river water in a golden bowl and was about to drink when it turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 孝恭曰：「盌中之血，公祏授首之祥。

translations.literal: Xiaogong said: "The blood in the bowl—an omen that Gongyu will lose his head.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong said: "The blood in the bowl is an omen that Gongyu will lose his head.

sentences.zh: 武德初，突厥國中雨血三日。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, in the Turks' country blood rained for three days.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude (618–619), in the Turks' lands blood rained for three days.

sentences.zh: 光宅初，宗室岐州刺史崇真之子橫、杭等夜宴，忽有氣如血腥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangye, sons Heng and Hang of Chongzhen, Prince of the imperial clan and prefect of Qizhou, held a night banquet when suddenly there was air like the smell of blood.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangye era (684), Heng, Hang, and the others—sons of Prince Chongzhen, prefect of Qizhou—held a night banquet when suddenly air like the smell of blood appeared.

sentences.zh: 武后時，來俊臣家井水變赤如血，井中夜有吁嗟歎惋聲，俊臣以木棧之，木忽自投十步外。

translations.literal: During the times of Empress Wu, at Lai Junchen's house the well water changed to red like blood; at night in the well there were sighing sounds of lament; Junchen blocked it with wood, and the wood suddenly cast itself ten paces away.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign, at Lai Junchen's house the well water turned red as blood; at night the well had sounds of sighing and lament; Junchen covered it with timbers, and the timber suddenly flung itself ten paces away.

sentences.zh: 長安中，幷州晉祠水赤如血。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, the waters of the Jin Shrine in Bingzhou were red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era (701–704), the waters of the Jin Shrine in Bingzhou were red as blood.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，成王千里家有血點地，及奩箱上有血淋瀝，腥聞數步。

translations.literal: During Zhongzong's reign, at Prince Qianli of Cheng's house blood spotted the ground, and on chests and boxes blood dripped profusely, smelled of stench for several paces.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhongzong's reign, at Prince Qianli of Cheng's house blood spotted the ground, and on chests and boxes blood dripped in profusion, its stench detectable for several paces.

sentences.zh: 又中郎將東夷人毛婆羅炊飯，一夕化為血。

translations.literal: Also the Eastern Yi man Mao Poluo, a commander of the palace guards, cooked rice—overnight it turned to blood.
translations.idiomatic: Also the Eastern Yi Mao Poluo, a commander of the palace guards, cooked rice that overnight turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年七月癸巳，赤氣際天，光燭地，三日乃止。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jinglong, on guisi, red vapor reached heaven, its light illuminating the earth; after three days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Jinglong (708), on guisi, red vapor reached heaven, its light illuminating the earth; after three days it stopped.

sentences.zh: 赤氣，血祥也。

translations.literal: Red vapor is an omen of blood.
translations.idiomatic: Red vapor is an omen of blood.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，少陵原楊慎矜父墓封域內，草木皆流血，慎矜令浮屠史敬思禳之，退朝裸而桎梏於叢棘間，如是數旬而流血不止。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, within the sealed bounds of the tomb of Yang Shenjin's father at Shaoling plain, all vegetation flowed blood; Shenjin had the Buddhist monk Shi Jingsi perform rites; he stripped naked and was shackled among thorn thickets; thus for several tens of days yet the bleeding did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao (747), within the sealed bounds of the tomb of Yang Shenjin's father at Shaoling Plain, all vegetation streamed blood; Shenjin had the Buddhist monk Shi Jingsi perform rites; stripped naked he was shackled among thorn thickets; thus for several tens of days yet the bleeding did not stop.

sentences.zh: 十二載，李林甫第東北隅每夜火光起，或有如小兒持火出入者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, at the northeast corner of Li Linfu's residence each night firelight arose, or like small children holding fire going in and out.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao (753), at the northeast corner of Li Linfu's residence firelight arose each night, or like small children bearing fire going in and out.

sentences.zh: 近赤祥也。

translations.literal: It nears red auspice.
translations.idiomatic: This approached red auspice.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年八月庚午夜，有赤光亙天，貫紫微，漸移東北，彌漫半天。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Baoying, on gengzi night, red light spanned heaven, piercing Ziwei, gradually moving northeast, flooding half the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi night in the eighth month of the first year of Baoying (762), red light spanned heaven, piercing Purple Tenuity, gradually shifting northeast and flooding half the sky.

sentences.zh: 大曆十三年二月，太僕寺有泥像，左臂上有黑汗滴下，以紙承之，血也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year of Dali, at the Imperial Stud there was a clay image; on its left arm black sweat dripped down—paper was placed to receive it, and it was blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year of Dali (778), at the Imperial Stud there was a clay image; black sweat dripped from its left arm—paper placed to receive it proved to be blood.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年十一月壬午，日沒，有赤氣五，出于黑雲中，亙天。

translations.literal: On renwu of the second year of Zhenyuan, the sun set; five red vapors issued from within black clouds and spanned heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the second year of Zhenyuan (786), at sunset five red vapors issued from within black clouds and spanned heaven.

sentences.zh: 十二年九月癸卯，夜有赤氣如火，見北方，上至北斗。

translations.literal: On guimao of the twelfth year, at night red vapor like fire appeared in the north, reaching up to the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao night in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan (796), red vapor like fire appeared in the north, reaching up to the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 十七年，福州劍池水赤如血。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the waters of the Sword Pool in Fuzhou were red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan (801), the waters of the Sword Pool in Fuzhou were red as blood.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月甲戌，雨赤雪于京師。

translations.literal: On jiaxu of the first month of the twenty-first year, red snow rained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the first month of the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan (805), red snow fell on the capital.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年二月，鄆州從事院門前地有血，方尺餘，色甚鮮赤，不知所從來，人以為自空而墮也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, before the gate of the Registrar's office in Yanzhou blood covered the ground, more than a square chi, color very fresh red—no one knew whence it came; people thought it fell from the void.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe (819), before the gate of the registrar's office in Yanzhou blood covered the ground, more than a square chi in extent, its color vividly red—no one knew whence it came; people thought it had fallen from the void.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年七月戊午，河水赤，三日止。

translations.literal: On wuwu of the seventh month of the first year of Changqing, the Yellow River turned red; after three days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the seventh month of the first year of Changqing (821), the Yellow River turned red; after three days it stopped.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年十二月乙酉夜，西北有霧起，須臾遍天，霧止，有赤氣，或淺或深，久而乃散。

translations.literal: On yiyou night of the twelfth month of the first year of Baoli, in the northwest mist arose; in a moment it filled heaven; when the mist stopped there was red vapor, sometimes pale sometimes deep, and after a long while it dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou night in the twelfth month of the first year of Baoli (825), in the northwest mist arose; in a moment it filled heaven; when the mist lifted there was red vapor, sometimes pale sometimes deep, and after a long while it dispersed.

sentences.zh: 大和元年四月庚戌，北方有赤氣，中有數白氣間之。

translations.literal: On gengxu of the fourth month of the first year of Dahe, in the north red vapor with several white vapors mingled among it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the fourth month of the first year of Dahe (827), in the north red vapor with several white vapors mingled among it.

sentences.zh: 六月乙卯夜，西北有赤氣。

translations.literal: On yimao night of the sixth month, in the northwest there was red vapor.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao night in the sixth month of the first year of Dahe (827), in the northwest there was red vapor.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，京師見赤氣滿天。

translations.literal: On guimao of the eighth month, in the capital red vapor filled heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eighth month of the first year of Dahe (827), in the capital red vapor filled heaven.

sentences.zh: 二年閏三月乙卯，北方有赤氣如血。

translations.literal: On yimao of the intercalary third month of the second year, in the north red vapor like blood.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the intercalary third month of the second year of Dahe (828), in the north red vapor like blood.

sentences.zh: 咸通七年，鄭州永福湖水赤如凝血者三日。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiantong, Yongfu Lake in Zhengzhou was red like congealed blood for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiantong (866), Yongfu Lake in Zhengzhou was red like congealed blood for three days.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，中書政事堂忽旦有死人，血汚滿地，不知主名。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu, at the Secretariat's Council Chamber at dawn suddenly there was a dead person, blood filth covering the ground, the master name unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qianfu (879), at the Secretariat's Council Chamber at dawn there suddenly lay a dead person, blood-stained filth covering the ground, the name of the victim unknown.

sentences.zh: 又御井水色赤而腥，渫之，得一死女子腐爛。

translations.literal: Also the imperial well water was red and foul; when drained, a dead woman rotting was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Also the imperial well water was red and foul; when drained, a rotting dead woman was found.

sentences.zh: 近赤祥也。

translations.literal: It nears red auspice.
translations.idiomatic: This approached red auspice.

sentences.zh: 中和二年七月丙午夜，西北方赤氣如絳，際天。

translations.literal: On bingzi night of the seventh month of the second year of Zhonghe, in the northwest red vapor like deep crimson reached heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi night in the seventh month of the second year of Zhonghe (882), in the northwest red vapor like deep crimson reached heaven.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年正月，潤州江水赤，凡數日。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Guangqi, the river waters of Runzhou turned red, altogether several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Guangqi (885), the river waters of Runzhou turned red for several days.

sentences.zh: 水沴火。

translations.literal: Water defiles fire.
translations.idiomatic: Water Defiles Fire

sentences.zh: 幽州坊谷地常有火，長慶三年夏，遂積水為池。

translations.literal: At Fang Valley in Youzhou fire was always present; in summer of the third year of Changqing, it finally accumulated water into a pool.
translations.idiomatic: At Fang Valley in Youzhou fire was always present; in the summer of the third year of Changqing (823), it finally accumulated into a pool of water.

sentences.zh: 近水沴火也。

translations.literal: It nears water defiling fire.
translations.idiomatic: This approached water defiling fire.
